title.zh: 卷一百九十八 列傳第一百四十八: 西戎
title.raw: 卷一百九十八 列傳第一百四十八: 西戎 Volume 198 Biographies 148: Western Regions

sentences.zh: 泥婆羅國

translations.literal: The Country of Nepal
translations.idiomatic: Nepal

sentences.zh: 泥婆羅國，在吐蕃西。

translations.literal: The country of Nepal is west of Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Nepal lay to the west of Tibet.

sentences.zh: 其俗翦髮與眉齊，穿耳，揎以竹桶牛角，綴至肩者以為姣麗。

translations.literal: Their custom is to cut the hair level with the eyebrows, pierce the ears, and insert bamboo tubes and ox horns; those that hang to the shoulders are considered beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they cropped their hair even with the eyebrows and pierced their ears, inserting bamboo tubes and ox horns as ornaments—those that dangled to the shoulders were regarded as especially lovely.

sentences.zh: 食用手，無匕箸。

translations.literal: They eat with the hands and have no spoons or chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: They ate with their hands and used neither spoons nor chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 其器皆銅。

translations.literal: Their vessels are all of bronze.
translations.idiomatic: All their tableware was made of bronze.

sentences.zh: 多商賈，少田作。

translations.literal: There are many merchants and few who work the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants were numerous, field labor scarce.

sentences.zh: 以銅為錢，面文為人，背文為馬牛，不穿孔。

translations.literal: They use bronze for money; the obverse bears the image of a man, the reverse that of horses and cattle, and they are not pierced.
translations.idiomatic: Their coinage was bronze, stamped on one side with a human figure and on the other with horses and cattle, without a central hole.

sentences.zh: 衣服以一幅蔽布身，日數盥浴。

translations.literal: For clothing they use a single breadth of cloth to cover the body, and they bathe several times a day.
translations.idiomatic: They wore a single length of cloth wrapped about the body and bathed many times each day.

sentences.zh: 以板為屋，壁皆雕畫。

translations.literal: They build houses of planks, and the walls are all carved and painted.
translations.idiomatic: Their houses were built of planks, every wall carved and painted.

sentences.zh: 俗重博戲，好吹蠡擊鼓。

translations.literal: The custom esteems gambling games and delights in blowing the li pipe and striking drums.
translations.idiomatic: They prized games of chance and delighted in wind instruments and drumming.

sentences.zh: 頗解推測盈虛，兼通歷術。

translations.literal: They are quite skilled at calculating surplus and deficit and also understand calendrical arts.
translations.idiomatic: They were adept at astronomical calculation and well versed in calendrical science.

sentences.zh: 事五天神，鐫石為像，每日清水浴神，烹羊而祭。

translations.literal: They serve the gods of the Five Heavens, carve stone into images, bathe the gods daily with clear water, and cook sheep as offerings.
translations.idiomatic: They worshipped the deities of the Five Heavens, carving stone images whom they bathed daily in fresh water and honored with boiled sheep.

sentences.zh: 其王那陵提婆，身著真珠、玻璃、車渠、珊瑚、琥珀、瓔珞，耳垂金鉤玉榼，佩寶裝伏突，坐獅子床，其堂內散花燃香。

translations.literal: Their king Narendradeva wore pearls, glass, lapis, coral, amber, and necklaces; golden hooks and jade cups hung from his ears; he wore a jeweled sword at his belt, sat on a lion throne, and within his hall flowers were scattered and incense burned.
translations.idiomatic: King Narendradeva was arrayed in pearls, crystal, lapis lazuli, coral, amber, and strings of gems; golden hooks and jade flasks hung from his ears, a jeweled blade at his waist. He sat upon a lion throne while flowers were strewn and incense burned in his hall.

sentences.zh: 大臣及諸左右並坐於地，持兵數百列侍其側。

translations.literal: Ministers and all attendants likewise sat on the ground, while several hundred men bearing weapons stood in ranks at his side.
translations.idiomatic: His ministers and attendants all sat upon the floor, while several hundred armed guards stood in ranks beside him.

sentences.zh: 宮中有七層之樓，覆以銅瓦，欄檻楹栿皆飾珠寶。

translations.literal: Within the palace was a seven-story tower roofed with bronze tiles; railings, pillars, and beams were all adorned with jewels.
translations.idiomatic: The palace contained a seven-tiered tower roofed in bronze tiles, its balustrades, pillars, and beams all inlaid with precious stones.

sentences.zh: 樓之四角，各懸銅槽，下有金龍，激水上樓，註於槽中，從龍口而出，狀若飛泉。

translations.literal: At each corner of the tower hung a bronze trough; below were golden dragons that pumped water up the tower into the troughs, whence it issued from the dragons' mouths like flying springs.
translations.idiomatic: At each corner of the tower hung a bronze channel; beneath stood golden dragons that drove water upward into the channels, whence it poured from the dragons' mouths in the likeness of cascading springs.

sentences.zh: 那陵提婆之父，為其叔父所篡，那陵提婆逃難於外，吐蕃因而納焉，克復其位，遂羈屬吐蕃。

translations.literal: Narendradeva's father was usurped by his uncle; Narendradeva fled into exile, and Tibet thereupon received him, restored him to his throne, and thus he came under Tibetan control.
translations.idiomatic: Narendradeva's father had been deposed by an uncle; the prince fled into exile, where Tibet took him in, helped him regain his throne, and thereafter held Nepal as a tributary state.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，衛尉丞李義表往使天竺，塗經其國，那陵提婆見之，大喜，與義表同出觀阿耆婆沴池。

translations.literal: During the Zhenguan reign, Vice Director of the Imperial Stud Li Yibiao was sent on a mission to India and passed through this country on the way; Narendradeva, upon seeing him, was greatly pleased and went out with Yibiao to view the Ajapala hot spring.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era, Vice Director of the Imperial Stud Li Yibiao traveled to India and passed through Nepal en route. Narendradeva was delighted to meet him and accompanied Yibiao to see the Ajapala hot spring.

sentences.zh: 周回二十余步，水恆沸，雖流潦暴集，爍石焦金，未嘗增減。

translations.literal: Its circumference was a little over twenty paces; the water was always boiling, and though torrents might pour in and stones glow and gold melt, it never increased or decreased.
translations.idiomatic: The pool measured a little over twenty paces around. Its waters boiled perpetually; even when floods poured in hot enough to make stone glow and metal run, the level never rose or fell.

sentences.zh: 以物投之，即生煙焰，懸釜而炊，須臾而熟。

translations.literal: If one cast something into it, smoke and flame would arise at once; suspend a pot and cook, and food is done in an instant.
translations.idiomatic: Cast anything into it and smoke and flame burst forth; hang a pot above it and a meal cooks in moments.

sentences.zh: 其後王玄策為天竺所掠，泥婆羅發騎與吐蕃共破天竺有功。

translations.literal: Later Wang Xuance was captured by India; Nepal sent cavalry and, together with Tibet, defeated India with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wang Xuance was seized in India, Nepal dispatched horsemen who, fighting alongside Tibet, helped defeat the Indians—a deed rewarded by the court.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年，其王屍利那連陀羅又遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui, their king Śrī Narendradeva again sent envoys to offer tribute at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yonghui (651), King Śrī Narendradeva again sent envoys bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 党項羌

translations.literal: The Tangut Qiang
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut (Dangxiang) Qiang

sentences.zh: 党項羌，在古析支之地，漢西羌之別種也。

translations.literal: The Tangut Qiang dwell in the ancient land of Qizhi and are a separate branch of the Western Qiang of Han times.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut Qiang inhabited the ancient territory of Qizhi and were a distinct branch of the Western Qiang known to the Han.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉之後，西羌微弱，或臣中國，或竄山野。

translations.literal: After the Wei and Jin dynasties the Western Qiang grew weak; some submitted to China, others fled into mountains and wilds.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei and Jin periods the Western Qiang had weakened—some submitted to the Chinese states, others scattered into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 自周氏滅宕昌、鄧至之後，党項始強。

translations.literal: After the Zhou house destroyed Dangchang and Dengzhi, the Tangut began to grow strong.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the Northern Zhou destroyed Dangchang and Dengzhi did the Tangut begin to rise in power.

sentences.zh: 其界東至松州，西接葉護，南雜舂桑、迷桑等羌，北連吐谷渾，處山谷間，互三千里。

translations.literal: Their borders reached Songzhou in the east, adjoined Yehu in the west, mingled in the south with the Chunsang, Misang, and other Qiang, and linked with Tuyuhun in the north; they dwelt among valleys and mountains across three thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Their territory extended east to Songzhou, west to the lands of Yehu, south among the Chunsang, Misang, and other Qiang peoples, and north to Tuyuhun—some three thousand li of mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 其種每姓別自為部落，一姓之中復分為小部落，大者萬余騎，小者數千騎，不相統一。

translations.literal: Each clan surname formed its own tribe; within one surname were again divided small tribes—the large had more than ten thousand horsemen, the small several thousand, and they were not unified.
translations.idiomatic: Each surname formed its own tribe, and within each surname smaller bands split off—the largest mustered more than ten thousand horsemen, the smallest several thousand, with no single authority over all.

sentences.zh: 有細封氏、費聽氏、往利氏、頗超氏、野辭氏、房當氏、米擒氏、拓拔氏，而拓拔最為強族。

translations.literal: There were the Xifeng, Feiting, Wangli, Pichao, Yeci, Fangdang, Miqin, and Tuoba clans, of whom the Tuoba were the strongest.
translations.idiomatic: Among their clans were the Xifeng, Feiting, Wangli, Pichao, Yeci, Fangdang, Miqin, and Tuoba—the Tuoba being the most powerful.

sentences.zh: 俗皆土著，居有棟宇，其屋織牦牛尾及羊毛覆之，每年一易。

translations.literal: By custom they were all settled agriculturists; their dwellings had beams and rafters, and their houses were thatched with woven yak tails and wool, replaced every year.
translations.idiomatic: They were sedentary, living in framed houses roofed with woven yak tails and wool that they replaced each year.

sentences.zh: 俗尚武，無法令賦役。

translations.literal: The custom esteems martial valor; there are no laws, taxes, or corvée.
translations.idiomatic: They valued martial prowess and knew neither written law nor regular taxation.

sentences.zh: 其人多壽，年一百五六十歲。

translations.literal: Their people are mostly long-lived, reaching one hundred fifty or sixty years.
translations.idiomatic: Many lived to a great age—one hundred fifty or even one hundred sixty years.

sentences.zh: 不事產業，好為盜竊，互相淩劫。

translations.literal: They do not engage in productive work but delight in theft and plunder one another.
translations.idiomatic: They did little honest labor and were fond of raiding and robbing one another.

sentences.zh: 尤重復仇，若仇人未得，必蓬頭垢面跣足蔬食，要斬仇人而後復常。

translations.literal: They especially esteem vengeance; if the enemy is not yet taken, they must go with disheveled hair, filthy faces, bare feet, and plain food, resolved to behead the foe before returning to normal life.
translations.idiomatic: Vengeance weighed above all: until an enemy was slain, a man went unkempt, barefoot, and abstinent, vowing to kill his foe before resuming ordinary life.

sentences.zh: 男女並衣裘褐，仍被大氈。

translations.literal: Men and women alike wear fur and coarse cloth and moreover wrap themselves in great felts.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women alike wore furs and coarse woolens, wrapped additionally in heavy felt cloaks.

sentences.zh: 畜牦牛、馬、驢、羊，以供其食。

translations.literal: They raise yaks, horses, donkeys, and sheep to supply their food.
translations.idiomatic: They kept yaks, horses, donkeys, and sheep for food.

sentences.zh: 不知稼穡，土無五谷。

translations.literal: They know nothing of planting and harvesting; the soil has none of the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: They did not farm; their land produced none of the staple grains.

sentences.zh: 氣候多風寒，五月草始生，八月霜雪降。

translations.literal: The climate is mostly windy and cold; grass begins to grow only in the fifth month, and frost and snow fall in the eighth.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was bitter and windy; grass scarcely appeared before the fifth month, and frost and snow came by the eighth.

sentences.zh: 求大麥於他界，醖以為酒。

translations.literal: They seek barley from other regions and ferment it into wine.
translations.idiomatic: They obtained barley from neighboring peoples and brewed it into wine.

sentences.zh: 妻其庶母及伯叔母、嫂、子弟之婦，淫穢烝褻，諸夷中最為甚，然不婚同姓。

translations.literal: They take as wives their stepmothers, paternal aunts by marriage, sisters-in-law, and the wives of younger brothers and sons—lewd and incestuous conduct most extreme among all the barbarians, yet they do not marry within the same surname.
translations.idiomatic: They married stepmothers, uncles' wives, sisters-in-law, and brothers' wives—practices more depraved than among any other frontier people, though they would not wed within the same clan name.

sentences.zh: 老死者以為盡天年，親戚不哭；

translations.literal: When the aged die, they are thought to have completed their heaven-allotted years, and kin do not weep;
translations.idiomatic: When the elderly died, kin took it as the completion of a full life and did not mourn;

sentences.zh: 少死者則雲夭枉，乃悲哭之。

translations.literal: when the young die, they say it is an untimely death, and then they mourn and weep.
translations.idiomatic: but when the young died, they called it a wrongful early death and wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 死則焚屍，名為火葬。

translations.literal: Upon death they burn the corpse, called fire burial.
translations.idiomatic: The dead were cremated in what they called fire burial.

sentences.zh: 無文字，但候草木以記歲時。

translations.literal: They have no writing but merely observe plants and trees to mark the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: They had no writing and reckoned the seasons only by watching when plants bloomed or withered.

sentences.zh: 三年一相聚，殺牛羊以祭天。

translations.literal: Every three years they gather together and slaughter cattle and sheep to sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years they assembled to slaughter cattle and sheep in sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 自周及隋，或叛或朝，常為邊患。

translations.literal: From the Zhou through the Sui, sometimes they rebelled and sometimes they came to court, constantly a border affliction.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhou through the Sui they alternately rebelled and submitted, a perennial trouble on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，南會州都督鄭元璹遣使招諭，其酋長細封步賴舉部內附，太宗降璽書慰撫之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan, Military Commissioner of Nanhui Prefecture Zheng Yuansui sent envoys to summon and instruct them; their chieftain Xifeng Bulai led his tribe to submit inwardly, and Taizong issued an imperial letter of seal-script to comfort and soothe him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenguan (629), Nanhui Prefecture commissioner Zheng Yuansui sent envoys to win them over. The chieftain Xifeng Bulai brought his people to submit, and Emperor Taizong sent a sealed letter of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 步賴因來朝，宴賜甚厚，列其地為軌州，拜步賴為刺史。

translations.literal: Bulai thereupon came to court; feasts and gifts were very generous; his land was established as Gui Prefecture, and Bulai was appointed prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Bulai came to court in person and received a lavish feast and gifts. His territory was organized as Gui Prefecture, and Bulai was named its prefect.

sentences.zh: 仍請率所部討吐谷渾。

translations.literal: He further requested to lead his followers to campaign against Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: He also offered to lead his tribesmen against Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 其後諸姓酋長相次率部落皆來內屬。

translations.literal: Afterward chieftains of the various surnames in succession led their tribes to come and submit inwardly.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter chieftains of the other clans brought their tribes to submit one after another.

sentences.zh: 請同編戶，太宗厚加撫慰，列其地為崌、奉、巖、遠四州，各拜其首領為刺史。

translations.literal: They requested to be registered like ordinary households; Taizong generously comforted them and established their lands as the four prefectures of Qi, Feng, Yan, and Yuan, appointing each leader as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: They asked to be registered as ordinary subjects. Taizong treated them generously, organizing their lands into the four prefectures of Qi, Feng, Yan, and Yuan and appointing each chieftain prefect.

sentences.zh: 有羌酋拓拔赤辭者，初臣屬吐谷渾，甚為渾主伏允所暱，與之結婚。

translations.literal: There was a Qiang chieftain Tuoba Chici who at first submitted to Tuyuhun and was greatly favored by the Tuyuhun ruler Fuyun, with whom he formed a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: One chieftain, Tuoba Chici, had initially submitted to Tuyuhun and was a favorite of King Fuyun, who gave him a princess in marriage.

sentences.zh: 及貞觀初，諸羌歸附，而赤辭不至。

translations.literal: When at the beginning of Zhenguan the various Qiang submitted, Chici did not come.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Zhenguan era, when the other Qiang submitted, Chici held back.

sentences.zh: 李靖之擊吐谷渾，赤辭屯狼道坡以抗官軍。

translations.literal: When Li Jing attacked Tuyuhun, Chici encamped at Langdao Slope to resist the government army.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing campaigned against Tuyuhun, Chici stationed his forces at Langdao Slope to block the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 廓州刺史久且洛生遣使諭以禍福，赤辭曰：「我被渾主親戚之恩，腹心相寄，生死不貳，焉知其他。

translations.literal: Guo Prefecture inspector Jiujie Luosheng sent envoys to explain fortune and disaster; Chici said: "I have received the Tuyuhun ruler's kindness as kin; he entrusted me with his innermost affairs; in life or death I am not double—how would I know anything else?
translations.idiomatic: Guo Prefecture inspector Jiujie Luosheng sent envoys to warn him of the consequences. Chici replied: "The Tuyuhun king has treated me as kin and entrusted me with his innermost counsel. I shall not waver in life or death—why should I heed anything else?

sentences.zh: 汝可速去，無令汙我刀也。」

translations.literal: You may go quickly—do not let my blade be stained by you.
translations.idiomatic: Be off at once, lest you stain my blade.

sentences.zh: 洛生知其不悟，於是率輕騎襲之，擊破赤辭於肅遠山，斬首數百級，虜雜畜六千而還。

translations.literal: Luosheng knew he would not come to his senses; he therefore led light cavalry in a surprise attack, defeated Chici at Mount Suyuan, took several hundred heads, and captured six thousand mixed livestock before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Chici would not listen, Luosheng led light cavalry in a surprise attack, routed him at Mount Suyuan, took several hundred heads, seized six thousand head of livestock, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太宗又令岷州都督李道彥說諭之，赤辭從子思頭密送誠款，其黨拓拔細豆又以所部來降。

translations.literal: Taizong again ordered Minzhou military commissioner Li Daoyan to persuade him; Chici's nephew Sitou secretly sent pledges of sincerity, and his follower Tuoba Xidou also came with his following to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then sent Minzhou commissioner Li Daoyan to negotiate. Chici's nephew Sitou secretly sent assurances of loyalty, and his follower Tuoba Xidou brought his band to surrender.

sentences.zh: 赤辭見其宗黨離，始有歸化之意。

translations.literal: Chici, seeing his clan and followers depart, first had the intention of submitting.
translations.idiomatic: When Chici saw his kin and followers slipping away, he at last considered submission.

sentences.zh: 後岷州都督劉師立復遣人招誘，於是與思頭並率眾內屬，拜赤辭為西戎州都督，賜姓李氏。

translations.literal: Later Minzhou commissioner Liu Shili again sent men to recruit and entice him; thereupon he and Sitou together led the masses to submit inwardly; Chici was appointed Military Commissioner of Xirong Prefecture and granted the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhou commissioner Liu Shili sent envoys again, and Chici and Sitou together led their people to submit. Chici was appointed commissioner of Xirong Prefecture and given the imperial surname Li.

sentences.zh: 自此職貢不絕。

translations.literal: From this time tribute and service did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: From then on their tribute missions never ceased.

sentences.zh: 其後吐蕃強盛，拓拔氏漸為所逼，遂請內徙，始移其部落於慶州，置靜邊等州以處之。

translations.literal: Afterward Tibet grew powerful; the Tuoba were gradually pressed by them, and they requested to move inward; their tribes were first relocated to Qingzhou, and Jingbian and other prefectures were established to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Tibet grew powerful, the Tuoba were increasingly squeezed and petitioned to move within the frontier. Their tribes were resettled in Qingzhou, with Jingbian and other prefectures established to receive them.

sentences.zh: 其故地陷於吐蕃，其處者為其役屬，吐蕃謂之「弭藥」。

translations.literal: Their former lands fell to Tibet; those who remained there became its subjects and servants; the Tibetans call them "Miyao."
translations.idiomatic: Their former homeland fell to Tibet; those who stayed behind became Tibetan subjects, whom the Tibetans called the Miyao.

sentences.zh: 又有黑党項，在於赤水之西。

translations.literal: There were also the Black Tangut, west of the Red Waters.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the Black Tangut, dwelling west of the Red River.

sentences.zh: 李靖之擊吐谷渾也，渾主伏允奔黑党項，居以空閑之地。

translations.literal: When Li Jing attacked Tuyuhun, the Tuyuhun ruler Fuyun fled to the Black Tangut, who gave him vacant land to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing struck Tuyuhun, King Fuyun fled to the Black Tangut, who granted him open pastureland.

sentences.zh: 及吐谷渾舉國內屬，黑党項酋長號敦善王因貢方物。

translations.literal: When Tuyuhun submitted with the whole state, the Black Tangut chieftain titled Dunshanwang thereupon presented local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: After Tuyuhun submitted en masse, the Black Tangut chieftain known as King Dunshan presented local goods in tribute.

sentences.zh: 又有雪山党項，姓破醜氏，居於雪山之下，及白狗、舂桑、白蘭等諸羌，自龍朔已後，並為吐蕃所破而臣屬焉。

translations.literal: There were also the Snow Mountain Tangut of the Pochou surname, dwelling below the snow mountains, and the White Dog, Chunsang, Bailan, and other Qiang—all from Longshuo onward were broken by Tibet and became its subjects.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the Snow Mountain Tangut of the Pochou clan, the White Dog, Chunsang, Bailan, and other Qiang bands—all of whom, from the Longshuo era onward, were defeated by Tibet and brought under its rule.

sentences.zh: 其在西北邊者，天授三年內附，凡二十萬口，分其地置朝、吳、浮、歸等十州，仍散居靈、夏等界內。

translations.literal: Those on the northwest border submitted inwardly in the third year of Tianshou—two hundred thousand persons in all; their land was divided and ten prefectures such as Chao, Wu, Fu, and Gui were established, and they were still scattered to dwell within the boundaries of Ling and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Those on the northwest frontier submitted in the third year of Tianshou (690)—some two hundred thousand people. Their territory was divided into ten prefectures including Chao, Wu, Fu, and Gui, while the people were settled among the Ling and Xia borderlands.

sentences.zh: 自至德已後，常為吐蕃所誘，密以官告授之，使為偵道，故時或侵叛，尋亦底寧。

translations.literal: From Zhide onward they were often enticed by Tibet, which secretly granted them official patents and made them scout routes; therefore they sometimes raided and rebelled, but soon were pacified again.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhide era (756–758) Tibet often won them over with secret commissions, using them as scouts—hence periodic raids and rebellions, soon quieted again.

sentences.zh: 寶應初，其首領來朝，請助國供靈州軍糧，優詔褒美。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoying their chieftain came to court, requesting to aid the state by supplying Lingzhou army grain; an excellent edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Baoying era (762) a chieftain came to court offering to supply grain for the Lingzhou garrison; an edict of praise was issued in reply.

sentences.zh: 其在涇、隴州界者，上元元年率其眾十余萬，詣鳳翔節度使崔光遠請降。

translations.literal: Those within the Jing and Long prefecture borders, in the first year of Shangyuan, led their masses of more than one hundred thousand to Fengxiang military commissioner Cui Guangyuan to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Those in the Jing and Long region, in the first year of Shangyuan (674), led more than one hundred thousand followers to Fengxiang commissioner Cui Guangyuan to surrender.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年十二月，其歸順州部落、乾封州部落、歸義州部落、順化州部落、和寧州部落、和義州部落、保善州部落、寧定州部落、羅雲州部落、朝鳳州部落，並詣山南西道都防禦使、梁州刺史臧希讓請州印。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Baoying, their tribes of Guishun, Qianfeng, Guiyi, Shunhua, Heping, Heyi, Baoshan, Ningding, Luoyun, and Chaofeng prefectures all went to the Defender-in-Chief of Southwest Shannan Circuit and Liangzhou inspector Zang Xirang to request prefectural seals.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the first year of Baoying (762), the tribes of Guishun, Qianfeng, Guiyi, Shunhua, Heping, Heyi, Baoshan, Ningding, Luoyun, and Chaofeng prefectures all went to Southwest Shannan defender and Liangzhou inspector Zang Xirang to request official prefectural seals.

sentences.zh: 希讓以聞，許之。

translations.literal: Xirang reported it and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xirang reported the request, and it was approved.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年十二月，初禁商賈以牛、馬、器械於党項部落貿易。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year of Zhenyuan, for the first time merchants were forbidden to trade cattle, horses, and weapons with Tangut tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the third year of Zhenyuan (787), the court first forbade merchants to trade cattle, horses, and weapons with Tangut tribes.

sentences.zh: 十五年二月，六州党項自石州奔過河西。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifteenth year, the six-prefecture Tangut fled from Shizhou across the river west of the He.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan (799), the six-prefecture Tangut fled from Shizhou across the Yellow River to the west.

sentences.zh: 党項有六府部落，曰野利越詩、野利龍兒、野利厥律、兒黃、野海、野窣等。

translations.literal: The Tangut had six-fu tribes called Yeliyueshi, Yelilong'er, Yelijuelü, Erhuang, Yehai, Yesu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut comprised six fu tribes: Yeliyueshi, Yelilong'er, Yelijuelü, Erhuang, Yehai, Yesu, and the like.

sentences.zh: 居慶州者號為東山部落，居夏州者號為平夏部落。

translations.literal: Those dwelling in Qingzhou were called the Eastern Mountain tribe; those in Xiazhou were called the Pingxia tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Those in Qingzhou were known as the Eastern Mountain tribe; those in Xiazhou as the Pingxia tribe.

sentences.zh: 永泰、大歷已後，居石州，依水草。

translations.literal: After Yongtai and Dali they dwelt in Shizhou, following grass and water.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongtai and Dali eras they had lived in Shizhou, following pasture and water.

sentences.zh: 至是永安城鎮將阿史那思昧擾其部落，求取駝馬無厭，中使又贊成其事，党項不堪其弊，遂率部落奔過河。

translations.literal: At this time Yong'an fortress garrison commander Ashina Simo harassed their tribes, demanding camels and horses without end; palace envoys moreover abetted the matter; the Tangut could not bear the abuse and therefore led their tribes to flee across the river.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Yong'an garrison commander Ashina Simo was harassing them, demanding camels and horses without limit, abetted by palace eunuchs. Unable to endure the exactions, the Tangut led their tribes across the river.

sentences.zh: 元和九年五月，復置宥州以護党項。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the ninth year of Yuanhe, You Prefecture was re-established to protect the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the ninth year of Yuanhe (814), You Prefecture was re-established to oversee the Tangut.

sentences.zh: 十五年十一月，命太子中允李寮為宣撫党項使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fifteenth year, Palace Attendant of the Heir Apparent Li Liao was appointed Commissioner for Pacification and Comfort of the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fifteenth year of Yuanhe (820), Li Liao, attendant to the heir apparent, was appointed commissioner to pacify the Tangut.

sentences.zh: 以部落繁富，時遠近商賈，賫繒貨入貿羊馬。

translations.literal: Because the tribes were numerous and prosperous, merchants from near and far at times brought silks and goods to trade for sheep and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribes had grown prosperous, and merchants from far and near brought silks and goods to trade for sheep and horses.

sentences.zh: 至太和、開成之際，其籓鎮統領無緒，恣其貪婪，不顧危亡，或強市其羊馬，不酬其直，以是部落苦之，遂相率為盜，靈、鹽之路小梗。

translations.literal: By the Taihe and Kaicheng period their frontier commanders' oversight was disorderly; they indulged greed without regard for peril; sometimes they forcibly bought sheep and horses and did not pay fair price—therefore the tribes suffered, and they banded together as bandits; the Ling and Yan roads were slightly obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: By the Taihe and Kaicheng eras (827–840) frontier commanders ruled without discipline, plundering recklessly—sometimes seizing sheep and horses by force without fair payment. The tribes, driven to desperation, turned to banditry in numbers, and traffic on the Ling and Yan routes was briefly disrupted.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，上頻命使安撫之，兼命憲臣為使，分三印以統之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huichang the emperor repeatedly ordered envoys to pacify them and also appointed censorial officials as commissioners, dividing three seals to oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Huichang era (841) the emperor repeatedly sent commissioners to pacify them, appointing censorial officials and dividing authority among three seals.

sentences.zh: 在邠、寧、延者，以侍御史、內供奉崔君會主之；

translations.literal: Those in Bin, Ning, and Yan were overseen by Attending Censor and Inner Attendant Cui Junhui;
translations.idiomatic: Attending censor and inner attendant Cui Junhui oversaw those in Bin, Ning, and Yan;

sentences.zh: 在鹽、夏、長、澤者，以侍御史、內供奉李鄠主之；

translations.literal: those in Yan, Xia, Chang, and Ze were overseen by Attending Censor and Inner Attendant Li E;
translations.idiomatic: attending censor and inner attendant Li E those in Yan, Xia, Chang, and Ze;

sentences.zh: 在靈、武、麟、勝者，以侍御史、內供奉鄭賀主之，仍各賜緋魚以重其事。

translations.literal: those in Ling, Wu, Lin, and Sheng were overseen by Attending Censor and Inner Attendant Zheng He; each was moreover granted crimson fish pouches to dignify the office.
translations.idiomatic: and attending censor and inner attendant Zheng He those in Ling, Wu, Lin, and Sheng—each granted the crimson fish insignia to mark the importance of the post.

sentences.zh: 久而無狀，尋皆罷之。

translations.literal: After long time without results, soon all were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After long service with little to show, all were soon dismissed.

sentences.zh: 高昌者，漢車師前王之庭，後漢戊己校尉之故地。

translations.literal: Gaochang is the court of the Former King of the Front Cheshi of Han and the old territory of the Wuji Colonel of the Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: Gaochang occupied the seat of the Former King of the Front Cheshi in Han times and the old domain of the Wuji Colonel under the Later Han.

sentences.zh: 在京師西四千三百里。

translations.literal: It is four thousand three hundred li west of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: It lay four thousand three hundred li west of the capital.

sentences.zh: 其國有二十一城，王都高昌。

translations.literal: The state has twenty-one cities; the royal capital is Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom comprised twenty-one cities, with Gaochang as the royal capital.

sentences.zh: 其交河城，前王庭也；

translations.literal: Its Jiaohe city was the former royal court;
translations.idiomatic: Jiaohe had been the earlier royal seat;

sentences.zh: 田地城，校尉城也。

translations.literal: Tiandi city was the colonel's city.
translations.idiomatic: and Tiandi the garrison city of the Han colonel.

sentences.zh: 勝兵且萬人。

translations.literal: Effective troops number nearly ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Its fighting strength approached ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 厥土良沃，谷麥歲再熟；

translations.literal: Its soil is fertile and good; grain and wheat ripen twice a year;
translations.idiomatic: The soil was rich; grain and wheat ripened twice a year;

sentences.zh: 有蒲萄酒，宜五果；

translations.literal: there is grape wine, and the five fruits flourish;
translations.idiomatic: there was grape wine and all manner of fruit;

sentences.zh: 有草名白疊，國人采其花，織以為布。

translations.literal: there is a plant called baidie; the people gather its flowers and weave them into cloth.
translations.idiomatic: and a plant called baidie whose flowers the people wove into cloth.

sentences.zh: 有文字，知書計，所置官亦采中國之號焉。

translations.literal: They have writing, understand accounts, and the offices they establish also adopt Chinese designations.
translations.idiomatic: They had a written language and kept accounts; their official titles followed Chinese models.

sentences.zh: 其王麹伯雅，即後魏時高昌王嘉之六世孫也。

translations.literal: Their king Qu Boya is the sixth-generation descendant of King Jia of Gaochang in the Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: King Qu Boya was the sixth-generation descendant of King Jia of Gaochang under the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝時入朝，拜左光祿大夫、車師太守、封弁國公，仍以戚屬宇文氏女為華容公主以妻之。

translations.literal: During Emperor Yang of Sui he came to court, was appointed Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Colonel of the Cheshi, enfeoffed as Duke of the Bian state, and moreover a daughter of the imperial clan surnamed Yuwen was made Princess of Huarong and given to him as wife.
translations.idiomatic: He had visited court under Emperor Yang of Sui and was appointed Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and colonel of Cheshi, enfeoffed as Duke of Bian, and given Princess Huarong of the imperial Yuwen clan in marriage.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，伯雅死，子文泰嗣，遣使來告哀，高祖遣前河州刺史硃惠表往吊之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude, Boya died; his son Wentai succeeded and sent envoys to announce mourning; Gaozu dispatched former Hezhou inspector Zhu Huibiao to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wude (619), Qu Boya died and his son Wentai succeeded him, sending envoys to announce the death. Emperor Gaozu sent former Hezhou inspector Zhu Huibiao to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 七年，文泰又獻狗雄雌各一，高六寸，長尺余，性甚慧，能曳馬銜燭，雲本出拂菻國。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Wentai again presented one male and one female dog, six inches tall and over a foot long, very clever, able to draw a horse bit and carry a candle; it is said they originally came from the land of Fulin.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (624), Wentai presented a male and female dog, each six inches tall and over a foot long—remarkably clever beasts that could draw a horse's bit and carry a candle. They were said to originate in Fulin (Byzantium).

sentences.zh: 中國有拂菻狗，自此始也。

translations.literal: China's Fulin dogs began from this.
translations.idiomatic: This was the first appearance in China of the famed Fulin lapdog.

sentences.zh: 太宗嗣位，復貢玄狐裘，因賜其妻宇文氏花鈿一具。

translations.literal: When Taizong succeeded the throne, he again offered tribute of black fox furs; Taizong thereupon granted his wife of the Yuwen clan a set of floral forehead ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong came to the throne, Wentai again sent black fox furs as tribute, and the emperor granted his Yuwen wife a set of floral forehead ornaments.

sentences.zh: 宇文氏復貢玉盤。

translations.literal: Lady Yuwen in turn presented a jade platter as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yuwen in turn sent a jade platter as tribute.

sentences.zh: 西域諸國所有動靜，輒以奏聞。

translations.literal: Whatever movements occurred among the states of the Western Regions, he would report them to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever happened among the Western Region states, he reported it to the court.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年冬，文泰來朝，及將歸蕃，賜遺甚厚。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of Zhenguan, Wentai came to court, and when he was about to return to his realm, gifts and send-offs were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year of Zhenguan (630), Wentai came to court; when he prepared to return home, the emperor lavished gifts upon him.

sentences.zh: 其妻宇文氏請預宗親，詔賜李氏，封常樂公主，下詔慰諭之。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Yuwen requested to be enrolled among the imperial clan; an edict granted her the surname Li, enfeoffed her as Princess of Changle, and issued an edict of comfort and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Yuwen asked to be enrolled among the imperial clan. An edict granted her the surname Li and the title Princess of Changle, with a letter of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 時西戎諸國來朝貢者，皆塗經高昌，文泰後稍壅絕之。

translations.literal: At that time the various Western Region states that came to offer tribute all passed through Gaochang on the way; Wentai afterward gradually blocked and cut them off.
translations.idiomatic: Western Region states bound for court all passed through Gaochang, but Wentai gradually began intercepting them.

sentences.zh: 伊吾先臣西突厥，至是內屬，文泰又與葉護連結，將擊伊吾。

translations.literal: Yiwu had first submitted to the Western Turks; at this time it submitted inwardly to China; Wentai again allied with the yabghu and was about to attack Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwu had once submitted to the Western Turks but now turned to China. Wentai allied with the Turkish yabghu and prepared to attack Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 太宗以其反覆，下書切讓，征其大臣冠軍阿史那矩入朝，將與議事。

translations.literal: Taizong, because of his fickleness, issued a letter of stern rebuke and summoned his minister Champion Ashina Ju to court to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong rebuked him sharply in writing and summoned his minister Ashina Ju to court for consultations.

sentences.zh: 文泰竟不遣，乃遣其長史麹雍來謝罪。

translations.literal: Wentai ultimately did not send him but instead dispatched his chief administrator Qu Yong to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Wentai refused to send Ju and instead dispatched his chief administrator Qu Yong to apologize.

sentences.zh: 初，大業之亂，中國人多投於突厥。

translations.literal: At first, during the disorders of the Daye era, many Chinese fled to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: During the disorders of the Daye era, many Chinese had fled to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 及頡利敗，或有奔高昌者，文泰皆拘留不遣。

translations.literal: When Jieli was defeated, some fled to Gaochang; Wentai detained them all and would not release them.
translations.idiomatic: After Jieli's defeat, some fled to Gaochang, and Wentai detained them all.

sentences.zh: 太宗詔令括送，文泰尚隱蔽之。

translations.literal: Taizong ordered them rounded up and sent back; Wentai still concealed them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong ordered them rounded up and returned, but Wentai still hid many away.

sentences.zh: 又尋與西突厥乙毗設擊破焉耆三城，虜其男女而去。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he again joined with the Western Turk Elibir she to smash three cities of Yanqi and carried off their men and women.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined the Western Turk Elibir she in attacking three Yanqi cities and carrying off their people.

sentences.zh: 焉耆王上表訴之，太宗遣虞部郎中李道裕往問其狀。

translations.literal: The king of Yanqi submitted a memorial of complaint; Taizong dispatched Bureau of Parks director Li Daoyu to investigate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Yanqi petitioned for redress, and Taizong sent Bureau of Parks director Li Daoyu to investigate.

sentences.zh: 十三年，太宗謂其使曰：「高昌數年來朝貢脫略，無籓臣禮，國中署置官號，準我百僚，稱臣於人，豈得如此！

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Taizong said to their envoy: "Gaochang in recent years has been lax in tribute and court attendance, without the rites of a vassal state; within the state offices and titles are established matching our hundred officials—how can one who calls himself subject to others act thus!
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (639), Taizong told their envoy: "For years Gaochang has neglected tribute and court attendance, ignoring the rites of a vassal. You set up offices matching our own bureaucracy—how can a subject of another power behave so!

sentences.zh: 今茲歲首，萬國來朝，而文泰不至。

translations.literal: Now at this year's beginning, ten thousand states come to court, yet Wentai does not come.
translations.idiomatic: At this New Year every state sent envoys—yet Wentai did not come.

sentences.zh: 增城深塹，預備討伐。

translations.literal: He adds walls and deep moats, preparing for punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He has raised his walls and deepened his moats, preparing for war.

sentences.zh: 日者我使人至彼，文泰云：『鷹飛於天，雉竄於蒿，貓遊於堂，鼠安於穴，各得其所，豈不活耶！』

translations.literal: Recently when my envoy reached there, Wentai said: 'The hawk flies in heaven, the pheasant hides in mugwort, the cat roams the hall, the rat rests in its hole—each has its place; are they not alive!
translations.idiomatic: When my envoy recently reached him, Wentai said: 'The hawk flies in heaven, the pheasant hides in the brush, the cat roams the hall, the rat rests in its hole—each in its place. Are they not alive?

sentences.zh: 又西域使欲來者，文泰悉拘留之。

translations.literal: Moreover envoys from the Western Regions wishing to come—Wentai detained them all.
translations.idiomatic: He has also detained every Western Region envoy trying to reach us.

sentences.zh: 又遣使謂薛延陀云：『既自為可汗，與漢天子敵也，何須拜謁其使。』

translations.literal: He also sent envoys telling the Xueyantuo: 'Since you have made yourself qaghan, you are equal to the Han Son of Heaven—why need you bow to his envoys?
translations.idiomatic: He sent word to the Xueyantuo: 'You have made yourself qaghan, equal to the Han emperor—why bow to his envoys?

sentences.zh: 事人闕禮，離間鄰好，惡而不誅，善者何勸？

translations.literal: In serving others he lacks rites, sows discord among neighbors—if evil is not punished, how are the good encouraged?
translations.idiomatic: He shows no courtesy to his betters and sows discord among neighbors. If evil goes unpunished, what encourages the good?

sentences.zh: 明年，當發兵馬以擊爾。」

translations.literal: Next year I shall dispatch troops and horses to attack you."
translations.idiomatic: Next year I shall send an army against you.

sentences.zh: 是時薛延陀可汗表請為軍向導，以擊高昌，太宗許之。

translations.literal: At this time the Xueyantuo qaghan memorialized requesting to serve as army guide to attack Gaochang; Taizong granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Xueyantuo qaghan then petitioned to guide the army against Gaochang, and Taizong agreed.

sentences.zh: 令民部尚書唐儉至延陀，與謀進取。

translations.literal: He ordered Minister of Revenue Tang Jian to go to the Xueyantuo to plan the advance.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Minister of Revenue Tang Jian to the Xueyantuo to coordinate the campaign.

sentences.zh: 太宗冀其悔過，復下璽書，示以禍福，征之入朝。

translations.literal: Taizong hoped he would repent; he again issued an imperial letter of seal-script, showing fortune and disaster, summoning him to court.
translations.idiomatic: Still hoping Wentai would repent, Taizong sent another sealed letter warning of consequences and summoning him to court.

sentences.zh: 文泰稱疾不至。

translations.literal: Wentai claimed illness and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Wentai pleaded illness and refused to come.

sentences.zh: 太宗乃命吏部尚書侯君集為交河道大總管，率左屯衛大將軍薛萬均及突厥、契、苾之眾，步騎數萬眾以擊之。

translations.literal: Taizong thereupon appointed Minister of Personnel Hou Junji as Grand Commander of the Jiaohe Circuit, leading Left Garrison Guard general Xue Wanjun and the masses of Turks, Qibi, and Tiele—several tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry—to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then appointed Minister of Personnel Hou Junji grand commander of the Jiaohe campaign, with Left Garrison Guard general Xue Wanjun and tens of thousands of Turkish, Qibi, and Tiele troops.

sentences.zh: 時公卿近臣，皆以行經沙磧，萬里用兵，恐難得誌；

translations.literal: At that time dukes, ministers, and close attendants all thought that marching through sandy wastes and waging war ten thousand li away would be hard to achieve their aim;
translations.idiomatic: Court officials objected that marching across the desert to fight ten thousand li away could not succeed;

sentences.zh: 又界居絕域，縱得之，不可以守，競以為諫。

translations.literal: moreover the border lay in a remote region—even if gained, it could not be held; they competed in offering remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: and even if won, the land could not be held. They remonstrated in chorus.

sentences.zh: 太宗皆不聽。

translations.literal: Taizong would not listen to any of them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong would hear none of it.

sentences.zh: 文泰謂所親曰：「吾往者朝覲，見秦、隴之北，城邑蕭條，非復有隋之比。

translations.literal: Wentai said to his intimates: "When I formerly attended court, I saw north of Qin and Long that cities and towns were desolate—not again like the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Wentai told his intimates: "When I last visited court, I saw how desolate the lands north of Qin and Long had become—nothing like Sui times.

sentences.zh: 設今伐我，發兵多則糧運不給；

translations.literal: Suppose they now attack me—if they send many troops, grain transport will not suffice;
translations.idiomatic: If they attack now, a large army cannot be supplied;

sentences.zh: 若發三萬以下，吾能制之。

translations.literal: if they send fewer than thirty thousand, I can control them.
translations.idiomatic: fewer than thirty thousand, and I can handle them.

sentences.zh: 加以磧路艱險，自然疲頓，吾以逸待勞，坐收其弊，何足為憂也？」

translations.literal: Moreover the desert route is hard and perilous—they will naturally grow weary; I wait at ease for their labor and sit to harvest their exhaustion—what is there to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: The desert march will exhaust them. I need only wait at ease while they wear themselves out. What is there to fear?

sentences.zh: 及聞王師臨磧口，惶駭計無所出，發病而死。

translations.literal: When he heard the imperial army had reached the desert pass, he was terrified and could devise no plan; he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned the imperial army had reached the desert pass, terror left him no recourse—he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 其子智盛嗣立。

translations.literal: His son Zhicheng succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhicheng succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 既而君集兵奄至柳谷，進趨田地城，將軍契苾何力為前軍，與之接戰而退。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Junji's army suddenly arrived at Willow Valley and advanced toward Tiandi city; General Qibi Heli served as vanguard, engaged in battle with them, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Junji's army soon appeared at Willow Valley and advanced on Tiandi. Vanguard general Qibi Heli skirmished and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 大軍繼之，攻拔其城，虜男女七千余口。

translations.literal: The main army followed, stormed and took the city, and captured more than seven thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: The main force followed, stormed the city, and took more than seven thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 進逼其都。

translations.literal: They advanced and pressed the capital.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed on toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 智盛移君集書曰：「有罪於天子者，先王也，咎深譴積，身已喪亡。

translations.literal: Zhicheng sent a letter to Junji saying: "The one guilty toward the Son of Heaven was the former king; blame and accumulated reproach were deep, and he has already perished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicheng wrote to Junji: "The one who offended the Son of Heaven was my father, who has already paid with his life.

sentences.zh: 智盛襲位無幾，君其赦諸？」

translations.literal: Zhicheng has inherited the throne only a short time—will you not pardon me?"
translations.idiomatic: I have only just succeeded him. Will you not show mercy?

sentences.zh: 君集謂曰：「若能悔禍，當面縛軍門也。」

translations.literal: Junji said: "If you can repent your calamity, you must come bound to the camp gate in person."
translations.idiomatic: Junji replied: "If you truly repent, come bound to my camp gate.

sentences.zh: 又命諸軍引沖車、拋車以逼之，飛石雨下，城中大懼。

translations.literal: He also ordered the armies to bring battering rams and catapults to press them; flying stones rained down, and great fear arose in the city.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered battering rams and catapults forward; stones rained down and panic seized the city.

sentences.zh: 智盛窮蹙，出城降。

translations.literal: Zhicheng, cornered, came out of the city and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Zhicheng came out and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 君集分兵掠地，下其三郡、五縣、二十二城。

translations.literal: Junji divided troops to overrun the land, taking three commanderies, five counties, and twenty-two cities.
translations.idiomatic: Junji sent columns to overrun the realm, taking three commanderies, five counties, and twenty-two cities.

sentences.zh: 戶八千，口三萬七千七百，馬四千三百匹。

translations.literal: Eight thousand households, thirty-seven thousand seven hundred persons, four thousand three hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: The tally: eight thousand households, thirty-seven thousand seven hundred people, and four thousand three hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 其界東西八百里，南北五百里。

translations.literal: Its borders were eight hundred li east to west and five hundred li north to south.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom measured eight hundred li east to west and five hundred li north to south.

sentences.zh: 先是，其國童謠云：「高昌兵馬如霜雪，漢家兵馬如日月。

translations.literal: Earlier, a children's song in the state said: "Gaochang's troops and horses are like frost and snow; the Han house's troops and horses are like sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: A children's song had foretold: "Gaochang's armies are frost and snow; the Han armies are sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 日月照霜雪，回手自消滅。」

translations.literal: Sun and moon shine on frost and snow—they turn their hands and it vanishes of itself."
translations.idiomatic: When sun and moon shine on frost and snow, it melts at a touch.

sentences.zh: 文泰使人捕其初唱者，不能得。

translations.literal: Wentai sent men to seize whoever first sang it but could not find them.
translations.idiomatic: Wentai had sent men to seize whoever first sang it, but none could be found.

sentences.zh: 初，文泰與西突厥欲谷設通和，遺其金帛，約有急相為表裏。

translations.literal: At first Wentai was on friendly terms with the Western Turk yabghu Elibir she, sent him gold and silks, and agreed that in emergency they would be outer and inner support to each other.
translations.idiomatic: Wentai had allied with the Western Turk yabghu Elibir she, sending gold and silks with a pact of mutual aid in crisis.

sentences.zh: 及聞君集兵至，欲谷設懼而西走，不敢救。

translations.literal: When he heard Junji's army had arrived, Elibir she was afraid and fled west, not daring to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When Junji's army arrived, Elibir she fled west in fear and dared not intervene.

sentences.zh: 君集尋遣使告捷，太宗大悅，宴白僚，班賜各有差。

translations.literal: Junji soon sent envoys to report victory; Taizong was greatly pleased, feasted the hundred officials, and distributed rewards each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Junji soon reported victory. Taizong was delighted, feasted his officials, and distributed rewards.

sentences.zh: 曲赦高昌部內從軍兵士已上，父子犯死罪已下，期親犯流已下，大功犯徒已下，小功緦麻犯杖罪，悉原之。

translations.literal: A partial amnesty was granted within Gaochang for soldiers who had served and above: father and son guilty of capital crime and below, relatives within mourning grades guilty of exile and below, those within greater merit grades guilty of penal servitude and below, those within lesser merit and hemp mourning grades guilty of beating— all were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: A partial amnesty covered Gaochang soldiers and their kin for crimes up to and including capital offenses among close relatives, exile among collateral kin, penal servitude among more distant kin, and corporal punishment among the most distant.

sentences.zh: 時太宗欲以高昌為州縣，特進魏征諫曰：「陛下初臨天下，高昌夫婦先來朝謁。

translations.literal: At that time Taizong wished to make Gaochang into prefectures and counties; Special Advancement Holder Wei Zheng remonstrated: "When Your Majesty first took the realm, the Gaochang couple came first to pay court.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong wished to annex Gaochang as prefectures and counties. Wei Zheng remonstrated: "When you first took the throne, the Gaochang king and queen came to court in person.

sentences.zh: 自後數月，商胡被其遏絕貢獻，加之不禮大國，遂使五誅載加。

translations.literal: Within a few months afterward, merchant foreigners were blocked from tribute by them; moreover they were disrespectful to the great state—thus the five punishments were heaped upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Within months they were blocking merchants and showing disrespect to the empire—hence the campaign of punishment.

sentences.zh: 若罪止文泰，斯亦可矣，未若撫其人而立其子，所謂伐罪吊民，威德被於遐外，為國之善者也。

translations.literal: If guilt stopped with Wentai, that would also do; better yet to comfort the people and establish his son—what is called punishing crime and consoling the people, with authority and virtue reaching distant regions, is the good of governing a state.
translations.idiomatic: If the guilt ended with Wentai, that would suffice. Better to comfort the people and install his son—punishing crime while succoring the people, spreading virtue to distant lands. That is true statecraft.

sentences.zh: 今若利其土壤，以為州縣，常須千余人鎮守，數年一易，每及交蕃，死者十有三四，遣辦衣資，離別親戚，十年之後，隴右空虛。

translations.literal: Now if you profit from their soil to make prefectures and counties, you will constantly need more than a thousand men to garrison; every few years they are rotated; whenever they cross the frontier, three or four in ten die; dispatching them to prepare clothing and supplies, parting from kin—after ten years Longyou will be emptied.
translations.idiomatic: If you seize their land for prefectures, you will need a thousand garrison troops rotated every few years. A third die crossing the frontier. After ten years Longyou will be drained of men and resources.

sentences.zh: 陛下終不得高昌撮谷尺布以助中國，所謂散有用而事無用，臣未見其可。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty in the end will not obtain from Gaochang even a handful of grain or a foot of cloth to aid China—what is called scattering the useful while undertaking the useless; your servant does not see how this can be done."
translations.idiomatic: You will never see a grain of Gaochang millet or a foot of its cloth aid China. You would scatter useful resources on a useless venture. I see no wisdom in it.

sentences.zh: 太宗不從，竟以其地置西州，又置安西都護府，留兵以鎮之。

translations.literal: Taizong did not follow this; he ultimately established their land as Xizhou and also set up the Protectorate General of the Pacified West, leaving troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong overruled him, established Xizhou and the Protectorate General of the Pacified West, and left troops to garrison the region.

sentences.zh: 初，西突厥遣其葉護，屯兵於可汗浮圖城，與高昌相影響，至是懼而來降，以其地為庭州。

translations.literal: At first the Western Turks sent their yabghu to station troops at Qaghan Buddha City, mutually supporting Gaochang; at this time, afraid, he came to surrender, and his land was made Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Turk yabghu had garrisoned Qaghan Buddha City in support of Gaochang; now, terrified, he surrendered, and his territory became Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 於是勒石紀功而旋。

translations.literal: Thereupon they carved stone to record merit and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They carved a victory stele and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 其智盛君臣及其豪右，皆徙中國。

translations.literal: Zhicheng, his ministers, and the powerful families were all relocated to China.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicheng, his court, and the leading families were all resettled within China.

sentences.zh: 麹氏有國，至智盛凡九世，一百三十四年而滅。

translations.literal: The Qu clan held the state; down to Zhicheng there were nine generations in all, one hundred thirty-four years, and then extinction.
translations.idiomatic: The Qu dynasty had ruled for nine generations over one hundred thirty-four years before its fall.

sentences.zh: 尋拜智盛為左武衛將軍，封金城郡公；

translations.literal: Soon Zhicheng was appointed General of the Left Martial Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Jincheng Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Zhicheng was soon appointed general of the Left Martial Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Jincheng;

sentences.zh: 弟智湛為右武衛中郎將，天山縣公。

translations.literal: his younger brother Zhizhan was made Middle General of the Right Martial Guard and Duke of Tianshan County.
translations.idiomatic: his brother Zhizhan became middle general of the Right Martial Guard and Duke of Tianshan.

sentences.zh: 及太宗崩，刊石像智盛之形，列於昭陵玄闕之下。

translations.literal: When Taizong died, a stone image of Zhicheng's form was carved and set below the Dark Gate of Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizong's death, a stone statue of Zhicheng was carved and placed below the Dark Gate of Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 智湛，麟德中終於左驍衛大將軍、西州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhizhan, in the Linde era, ended his career as Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry and Inspector of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhan died in the Linde era as grand general of the Left Valiant Cavalry and inspector of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 天授初，其子崇裕授左武衛大將軍，交阿郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshou, his son Chongyu was appointed Grand General of the Left Martial Guard and King of the Jiao'a Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianshou era, his son Chongyu was appointed grand general of the Left Martial Guard and King of Jiao'a.

sentences.zh: 卒，封襲遂絕。

translations.literal: He died, and the enfeoffment and succession came to an end.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the line of enfeoffment ended.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾

translations.literal: Tuyuhun
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾，其先居於徒河之清山，屬晉亂，始度隴，止於甘松之南，洮水之西，南極白蘭，地數千里。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun—their ancestors dwelt at Clear Mountain on the Tuo River; during the disorders of Jin they first crossed Long, stopping south of Gansong and west of the Tao River, reaching south to Bailan, a territory of several thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun originally lived at Clear Mountain on the Tuo River. During the Jin disorders they crossed Long into the region south of Gansong and west of the Tao River, extending south to Bailan—a domain of several thousand li.

sentences.zh: 有城郭而不居，隨逐水草，廬帳為室，肉酪為糧。

translations.literal: They had walled towns but did not dwell in them; they followed grass and water, made felt tents their dwellings, and meat and curds their food.
translations.idiomatic: They had walled towns but did not live in them, following pasture and water, dwelling in felt tents and living on meat and curds.

sentences.zh: 其官初有長史、司馬、將軍。

translations.literal: Their offices at first had chief administrators, marshals, and generals.
translations.idiomatic: Their government at first had chief administrators, marshals, and generals.

sentences.zh: 近代已來，有王公、僕射、尚書、郎中。

translations.literal: In recent times there have been princes, dukes, vice premiers, ministers, and directors.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times they added princes, dukes, vice premiers, ministers, and directors.

sentences.zh: 其俗頗識文字。

translations.literal: Their custom is fairly literate.
translations.idiomatic: They were fairly literate.

sentences.zh: 男子通服長裙繒帽，或戴冪苾，婦人以金花為首飾，辮髮縈後，綴以珠貝。

translations.literal: Men generally wore long skirts, silk caps, or sometimes wore felt hoods; women used golden flowers as head ornaments, braided hair wound behind, adorned with pearls and shells.
translations.idiomatic: Men wore long skirts and silk caps, sometimes felt hoods. Women adorned their braided hair with golden flowers, pearls, and shells.

sentences.zh: 其婚姻富家厚出聘財，貧人竊女而去。

translations.literal: In marriage the wealthy give lavish betrothal gifts; the poor steal girls and carry them off.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy families paid lavish bride-prices; the poor simply abducted brides.

sentences.zh: 父卒，妻其庶母；

translations.literal: When the father dies, they marry his concubines;
translations.idiomatic: Upon a father's death, a son married his stepmothers;

sentences.zh: 兄亡，妻其諸嫂。

translations.literal: when the elder brother dies, they marry his sisters-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: upon a brother's death, his brothers married the widows.

sentences.zh: 喪有服制，葬訖而除。

translations.literal: Mourning has garment regulations; when burial is finished, mourning is removed.
translations.idiomatic: They observed mourning garments until burial, then ended mourning.

sentences.zh: 國無常稅，用度不給，輒斂富室商人，以取足而止。

translations.literal: The state has no regular taxes; when expenditures are insufficient, they levy wealthy households and merchants until enough is obtained and then stop.
translations.idiomatic: There were no regular taxes; when funds ran short, they levied the wealthy and merchants until enough was raised.

sentences.zh: 殺人及盜馬者罪死，他犯則征物以贖罪。

translations.literal: Murderers and horse thieves are punished with death; other offenses are redeemed by levying goods.
translations.idiomatic: Murder and horse theft were capital crimes; lesser offenses were redeemed with goods.

sentences.zh: 氣候多寒，土宜大麥、蔓菁，頗有菽粟。

translations.literal: The climate is mostly cold; the soil suits barley and turnips, and there is a fair amount of beans and millet.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was cold; barley and turnips flourished, with some beans and millet.

sentences.zh: 出良馬、牦牛、銅、鐵、硃砂之類。

translations.literal: They produce fine horses, yaks, copper, iron, cinnabar, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: They produced fine horses, yaks, copper, iron, cinnabar, and the like.

sentences.zh: 有青海，周回八百里，中有小山，至冬，放牝馬於其上，言得龍種。

translations.literal: There is Qinghai Lake, eight hundred li in circumference; within it is a small hill; in winter they release brood mares upon it, saying they obtain dragon stock.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghai Lake measured eight hundred li around, with a small hill in its midst. Each winter they turned brood mares loose upon it, claiming they bred with dragons.

sentences.zh: 嘗得波斯馬，放入海，因生驄駒，能日行千里，故代稱「青海驄」焉。

translations.literal: They once obtained Persian horses and released them into the lake; thus were born piebald colts able to travel a thousand li in a day—hence for generations they have been called "Qinghai piebalds."
translations.idiomatic: They once bred Persian stallions with these mares, producing piebald colts said to run a thousand li a day—the famed Qinghai piebalds.

sentences.zh: 地兼鄯善、且沫。

translations.literal: Their territory included Shanshan and Qiemo.
translations.idiomatic: Their territory included Shanshan and Qiemo.

sentences.zh: 西北有流沙數百里，夏有熱風，傷弊行旅，風之將至，老駝便知之，則引項而鳴，以口鼻埋沙中。

translations.literal: To the northwest are drifting sands several hundred li; in summer there are hot winds that harm travelers; when the wind is about to come, old camels know it, stretch their necks and cry, and bury muzzle and nostrils in the sand.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest lay drifting sands hundreds of li across. Summer brought killing hot winds; old camels sensed them coming, stretched their necks and bellowed, and buried their muzzles in the sand.

sentences.zh: 人以為候，即以氈擁蔽口鼻而避其患。

translations.literal: People take this as a sign and then use felt to cover and shield mouth and nose to avoid the harm.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers took this as warning and wrapped felt over their faces to survive.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝時，其王伏允來犯塞，煬帝親總六軍以討之，伏允以數十騎潛於泥嶺而遁，其仙頭王率男女十余萬口來降。

translations.literal: During Emperor Yang of Sui, their king Fuyun came to raid the frontier; Emperor Yang personally commanded the Six Armies to campaign against him; Fuyun with several dozen horsemen slipped away through Ni Ridge, while his Xiantou king led more than one hundred thousand men and women to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang, King Fuyun raided the frontier. The emperor led the Six Armies in person; Fuyun escaped through Ni Ridge with a few dozen riders while his Xiantou king surrendered with more than one hundred thousand people.

sentences.zh: 煬帝立其質子順為王，送之本國，令統余眾，尋復追還。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang established his hostage Shun as king, sent him to his native state to command the remaining masses, but soon recalled him again.
translations.idiomatic: Yang installed his hostage Shun as king and sent him home to rule the remnant, but soon recalled him.

sentences.zh: 大業末，伏允悉收故地，復為邊患。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye, Fuyun recovered all the old territory and again became a border affliction.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Daye era, Fuyun had recovered all his old territory and again troubled the frontier.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，順自江都來歸長安。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Shun came from Jiangdu to return to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Shun came from Jiangdu to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 時李軌猶據涼州，高祖遣使與伏允通和，令擊軌以自效，當放順返國。

translations.literal: At that time Li Gui still held Liangzhou; Gaozu sent envoys to treat peacefully with Fuyun, ordering him to attack Gui to prove his merit, whereupon Shun would be released to return to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui still held Liangzhou. Gaozu sent envoys to Fuyun, promising to return Shun if Fuyun attacked Li Gui.

sentences.zh: 伏允大悅，興兵擊之，戰於庫門，交綏而退。

translations.literal: Fuyun was greatly pleased, raised troops to attack him, fought at Kumen, exchanged blows and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyun was delighted, marched against Li Gui, fought at Kumen, and withdrew after an indecisive clash.

sentences.zh: 頻遣使朝貢，以順為請，高祖乃遣之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sent envoys with tribute, requesting Shun; Gaozu thereupon sent him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent frequent tribute missions asking for Shun's return, and Gaozu finally sent him home.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，伏允遣其洛陽公來朝。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Fuyun sent his Duke of Luoyang to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong came to the throne, Fuyun sent his Duke of Luoyang to pay court.

sentences.zh: 使未返，大掠鄯州而去。

translations.literal: Before the envoy returned, he plundered Shan Prefecture on a great scale and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Before the envoy had even returned home, Fuyun launched a major raid on Shan Prefecture and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣使責讓之，征伏允入朝，稱疾不至。

translations.literal: Taizong sent envoys to reproach him, summoned Fuyun to court, and he claimed illness and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent envoys to rebuke him and summoned Fuyun to court, but Fuyun pleaded illness and refused to come.

sentences.zh: 仍為其子尊王求婚，於是責其親迎以羈縻之。

translations.literal: He further sought a marriage alliance for his son Prince Zun; thereupon the court required him to come in person to escort the bride as a means of control.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyun also asked that his son Prince Zun be granted a marriage alliance, whereupon the court insisted that he come in person to escort the bride—a move intended to keep him under control.

sentences.zh: 尊王又稱疾不肯入朝，有詔停婚，遣中郎將康處直諭以禍福。

translations.literal: Prince Zun again claimed illness and refused to come to court; an edict halted the marriage, and Central Commandant Kang Chuzhi was sent to explain fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zun again pleaded illness and would not come to court. An edict canceled the marriage, and Central Commandant Kang Chuzhi was dispatched to spell out the consequences.

sentences.zh: 伏允遣兵寇蘭、廓二州。

translations.literal: Fuyun sent troops to raid Lan and Kuo prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyun sent troops to raid Lan and Kuo prefectures.

sentences.zh: 時鄯州刺史李玄運上言：「吐谷渾良馬悉牧青海，輕兵掩之，可致大利。」

translations.literal: At that time Shan Prefecture inspector Li Xuanyun memorialized: "Tuyuhun's fine horses are all pastured at Qinghai; light troops could surprise them and achieve great profit.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Xuanyun, inspector of Shan Prefecture, memorialized: "All of Tuyuhun's best horses are pastured at Qinghai Lake. A light strike force could take them by surprise and win a great prize.

sentences.zh: 於是遣左驍衛大將軍段誌玄率邊兵及契苾、党項之眾以擊之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the court sent Left Xiao-wei Grand General Duan Zhixuan leading frontier troops and the forces of the Qibi and Tangut to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The court thereupon dispatched Duan Zhixuan, Grand General of the Left Xiao-wei Guard, with frontier troops and Qibi and Tangut auxiliaries to attack them.

sentences.zh: 去青海三十里，誌玄與左驍衛將軍梁洛仁不欲戰，頓軍遲留不進，吐谷渾遂驅青海牧馬而遁。

translations.literal: Thirty li from Qinghai, Zhixuan and Left Xiao-wei General Liang Luoren did not wish to fight, halted the army and lingered without advancing; Tuyuhun then drove off the Qinghai pastured horses and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty li from Qinghai Lake, Zhixuan and Liang Luoren of the Left Xiao-wei Guard hung back and refused to fight. Tuyuhun drove off the horses pastured at Qinghai and escaped.

sentences.zh: 亞將李君羨率精騎別路，及賊於青海之南懸水鎮，擊破之，虜牛羊二萬余頭而還。

translations.literal: Deputy commander Li Junxian led elite cavalry by a separate route, caught the bandits at Xuanshui Town south of Qinghai, defeated them, and returned with more than twenty thousand head of cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander Li Junxian took a separate route with elite cavalry, caught the enemy at Xuanshui Town south of Qinghai Lake, routed them, and returned with more than twenty thousand head of cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 時伏允年老昏耄，其邪臣天柱王惑亂之，拘我行人鴻臚丞趙德楷。

translations.literal: At that time Fuyun was old and senile; his wicked minister Tianzhu Wang confused and disrupted him and detained our traveling envoy Herald Vice Director Zhao Dekai.
translations.idiomatic: By then Fuyun was old and failing. His wicked minister Tianzhu Wang misled him and had Zhao Dekai, Vice Director of the Herald's Office and imperial envoy, seized and detained.

sentences.zh: 太宗頻遣宣諭，使者十余返，竟無悛心。

translations.literal: Taizong repeatedly sent envoys to instruct him; more than ten missions returned, yet in the end he showed no sign of repentance.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent envoy after envoy to reason with him. More than ten missions came and went, yet Fuyun never showed the slightest sign of reform.

sentences.zh: 貞觀九年，詔特進李靖為西海道行軍大總管；

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenguan, an edict appointed Special Advancement Li Jing as Grand Commander of the Western Sea Route campaign army;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhenguan, Li Jing was appointed Special Advancement and Grand Commander of the Western Sea Route campaign army;

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書侯君集為積石道行軍總管，任城王道宗為鄯州道行軍總管，仍為靖副；

translations.literal: Minister of War Hou Junji as Route Commander of the Jishi Route campaign army, Prince Daizong of Rencheng as Route Commander of the Shanzhou Route campaign army, also serving as Li Jing's deputy;
translations.idiomatic: Hou Junji, Minister of War, as Route Commander of the Jishi Route; Prince Daizong of Rencheng as Route Commander of the Shanzhou Route and Li Jing's deputy;

sentences.zh: 涼州都督李大亮為且沫道行軍總管，岷州都督李道彥為赤水道行軍總管，利州刺史高甑生為鹽澤道行軍總管，並突厥、契苾之眾以擊之。

translations.literal: Liangzhou Protector-General Li Daliang as Route Commander of the Qiemo Route campaign army, Minzhou Protector-General Li Daoyan as Route Commander of the Chishui Route campaign army, Lizhou prefect Gao Zengsheng as Route Commander of the Yanzhe Route campaign army—all with Turkic and Qibi forces to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daliang, Protector-General of Liangzhou, on the Qiemo Route; Li Daoyan, Protector-General of Minzhou, on the Chishui Route; and Gao Zengsheng, prefect of Lizhou, on the Yanzhe Route—all with Turkic and Qibi auxiliaries to strike Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 諸將頻與賊遇，連戰破之，獲其高昌王慕容孝雋。

translations.literal: The generals frequently encountered the bandits, defeated them in successive battles, and captured their Gaochang king Murong Xiaojun.
translations.idiomatic: The generals met the enemy again and again, winning battle after battle, and captured Murong Xiaojun, king of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 孝雋有雄略，伏允心膂之臣也。

translations.literal: Xiaojun had bold strategy; he was a close confidant of Fuyun.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaojun was a man of bold strategy and one of Fuyun's most trusted advisers.

sentences.zh: 靖等進至赤海，遇其天柱三部落，擊大破之，遂歷於河源。

translations.literal: Li Jing and the others advanced to Red Sea, encountered the three tribes of Tianzhu, defeated them utterly, and then passed through the Yellow River source region.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing and his commanders pushed on to Red Sea, smashed the three Tianzhu tribes, and then marched through the region of the Yellow River's source.

sentences.zh: 李大亮又俘其名王二十人，雜畜數萬，至且沫西境，或傳伏允西走，渡圖倫磧，欲入於闐。

translations.literal: Li Daliang also captured twenty of their noble kings and tens of thousands of mixed livestock; reaching the western border of Qiemo, it was reported that Fuyun had fled west, crossing the Tulun Desert, intending to enter Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daliang captured twenty Tuyuhun noble kings and tens of thousands of livestock. At the western edge of Qiemo, word came that Fuyun had fled west across the Tulun Desert, aiming to reach Khotan.

sentences.zh: 將軍薛萬均率輕銳追奔，入磧數百里，及其余黨，破之。

translations.literal: General Xue Wanjun led light crack troops in pursuit, entered the desert several hundred li, caught up with the remnant band, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: General Xue Wanjun led light crack troops in pursuit, plunged several hundred li into the desert, overtook the fleeing remnant, and destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 磧中乏水，將士皆刺馬血而飲之。

translations.literal: Water was scarce in the desert; officers and soldiers all pierced their horses and drank the blood.
translations.idiomatic: Water ran out in the desert, and officers and soldiers pierced their horses and drank the blood to survive.

sentences.zh: 侯君集與江夏王道宗趣南路，登漢哭山，飲馬烏海，獲其名王梁屈忽，經塗二千餘里空虛之地，盛夏降霜，多積雪，其地乏水草，將士啖冰，馬皆食雪。

translations.literal: Hou Junji and Prince Daozong of Jiangxia took the southern route, ascended Mount Hanku, watered their horses at Wuhai, captured the noble king Liang Quhu; crossing more than two thousand li of empty land, in midsummer frost fell, snow accumulated heavily, the ground lacked water and fodder, officers and soldiers ate ice, and the horses all fed on snow.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Junji and Prince Daozong of Jiangxia took the southern route, climbed Mount Hanku, watered their horses at Wuhai, and captured the noble king Liang Quhu. They crossed more than two thousand li of empty wasteland where frost fell even in midsummer and snow lay deep. With no water or fodder, the men ate ice and the horses fed on snow.

sentences.zh: 又達於柏梁，北望積石山，觀河源之所出焉。

translations.literal: They also reached Bailiang, gazed north at Jishi Mountain, and observed where the Yellow River source issued forth.
translations.idiomatic: They also reached Bailiang, looked north toward Jishi Mountain, and beheld the place where the Yellow River rises.

sentences.zh: 兩軍會於大非川，至破邏貞谷，伏允子大寧王順窮蹙，斬其國相天柱王，舉國來降。

translations.literal: The two armies united at Great Non River, reaching Poluo Valley; Fuyun's son, Great Tranquility King Shun, was hard pressed, beheaded the state counselor Tianzhu Wang, and submitted with the whole nation.
translations.idiomatic: The two armies joined at the Great Non River and pushed on to Poluo Valley. Fuyun's son, Great Tranquility King Shun, was driven to desperation, executed the state counselor Tianzhu Wang, and surrendered with the whole kingdom.

sentences.zh: 伏允大懼，與千余騎遁於磧中，眾稍亡散，能屬之者才百余騎，乃自縊而死。

translations.literal: Fuyun was greatly afraid; with more than a thousand horsemen he fled into the desert, his followers gradually scattered—only a little over a hundred riders remained with him—and he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyun was terrified. He fled into the desert with a thousand riders, but his followers steadily deserted him until barely a hundred remained. Then he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 國人乃立順為可汗，稱臣內附。

translations.literal: The people thereupon enthroned Shun as khan and submitted as vassals within the empire.
translations.idiomatic: The people then enthroned Shun as khan and submitted to the Tang as vassals.

sentences.zh: 順，即伏允之嫡子也。

translations.literal: Shun was Fuyun's eldest son by the principal wife.
translations.idiomatic: Shun was Fuyun's eldest son by his principal wife.

sentences.zh: 初為侍子於隋，拜金紫光祿大夫，久不得歸，伏允遂立他子為太子，及得返國，意常怏怏。

translations.literal: Initially he had served as hostage at the Sui court, receiving appointment as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; long unable to return, Fuyun then established another son as crown prince—when he finally returned to his homeland, he was constantly resentful.
translations.idiomatic: He had first served as a hostage at the Sui court and been made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon. Kept away for years, he could not return home; Fuyun had meanwhile named another son crown prince. When Shun finally came back, he remained bitter at heart.

sentences.zh: 會李靖等諸軍所向克捷，自以失位，欲因此立功，由是遂降。

translations.literal: When Li Jing and the other armies won victory wherever they marched, he considered himself displaced and wished thereby to achieve merit—therefore he submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing's armies began winning everywhere, Shun saw that he had lost his place at court and hoped to redeem himself through merit. That was why he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 乃詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict thereupon stated:
translations.idiomatic: An edict thereupon stated:

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾擅相君長，竊據荒裔，誌在兇德，政出權門。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun presumptuously chose their own ruler, seized a remote borderland, their ambition lay in wicked conduct, and government issued from powerful factions.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun had presumptuously chosen their own rulers, seized a remote frontier, set their hearts on wicked deeds, and let power pass through factional hands.

sentences.zh: 酋渠攜貳，種落怨憤，長惡不悛，野心彌熾。

translations.literal: Their chieftains turned disloyal, the tribes grew angry and resentful, persisting in evil without reform, their wild ambition ever fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Their chieftains turned disloyal, the tribes seethed with anger, they persisted in evil without reform, and their wild ambitions burned ever hotter.

sentences.zh: 莫顧籓臣之禮，曾無事上之節，草竊疆場，虐割兆庶，積惡既稔，天亡有征。

translations.literal: They disregarded the rites owed a frontier vassal and showed not the least deference to the sovereign, raiding the borders and cruelly harming the people; their accumulated wickedness ripe, Heaven's destruction had its sign.
translations.idiomatic: They ignored the duties of a frontier vassal and showed no deference to the throne, raiding the borders and cruelly preying on the people. Their wickedness had ripened, and Heaven's judgment was already at hand.

sentences.zh: 朕君臨四海，含育萬類，一物失所，責深在予。

translations.literal: We rule the four seas and nurture all beings—when a single creature suffers loss, the blame lies deeply with Us.
translations.idiomatic: We rule the four seas and nurture every living thing; when even one creature suffers harm, the fault lies deeply with Us.

sentences.zh: 所以爰命六軍，申茲九伐，義存活國，情非黷武。

translations.literal: Therefore We hereby command the Six Armies and proclaim this punitive campaign, acting in righteousness to preserve the state, not from any love of warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore We have ordered the Six Armies forth and proclaimed this righteous punitive campaign—not from any love of war, but to preserve the realm in justice.

sentences.zh: 其子大寧王慕容順，隋氏之甥，誌懷明悟，長自中土，幸慕華風，爰見時機，深識逆順。

translations.literal: His son, Great Tranquility King Murong Shun, a nephew of the House of Sui, is intelligent in mind, grew up in the Central Plains, gladly admires civilized custom, recognized the moment, and deeply understood right and wrong.
