translations.idiomatic: His son, Great Tranquility King Murong Shun, a nephew of the House of Sui, is clear-minded and quick to understand. Raised in the Central Plains, he gladly admired civilized ways, saw the moment for what it was, and understood clearly which course was right.

sentences.zh: 以其愎諫違眾，獨陷迷途，遂誅邪臣，存茲大計。

translations.literal: Because his obstinate counsel defied the multitude and he alone strayed onto a wrong path, he then executed the wicked minister and preserved this great design.
translations.idiomatic: Though his stubborn counsel once defied the people and led him astray, he then executed the wicked minister and preserved the greater design.

sentences.zh: 翻然改轍，代父歸罪，忠孝之美，深有可嘉。

translations.literal: Turning abruptly from his former course, he took guilt upon himself in his father's stead—the beauty of filial loyalty is truly worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: He turned sharply from his former course, took guilt upon himself in his father's place, and in that union of loyalty and filial duty showed merit truly worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 子能立功，足以補過，既往之釁，特宜原免。

translations.literal: A son who can achieve merit suffices to redeem faults; past offenses should especially be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: When a son can achieve merit, that is enough to redeem past faults; his earlier offenses should therefore be specially forgiven.

sentences.zh: 然其建國西鄙，已歷年代，即從廢絕，情所未忍，繼其宗祀，允歸命胤。

translations.literal: Yet they founded a state on the western marches and it has endured through generations—to cut it off entirely Our heart cannot bear it; to continue their ancestral rites, fittingly he shall receive the mandate as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they founded a state on the western marches that had endured for generations. To cut it off entirely Our heart cannot bear; to continue their ancestral rites, fittingly the mandate should pass to this heir.

sentences.zh: 可封順為西平郡王，仍授趉胡呂烏甘豆可汗。

translations.literal: Shun may be enfeoffed as Prince of Xiping Commandery and further invested as Khan Tuohulu Wugandou.
translations.idiomatic: Shun is to be enfeoffed as Prince of Xiping Commandery and further invested as Khan Tuohulu Wugandou.

sentences.zh: 太宗恐順不能靜其國，仍遣李大亮率精兵數千，為其聲援。

translations.literal: Taizong feared Shun could not pacify his state and still sent Li Daliang with several thousand elite troops as backing.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong feared that Shun could not pacify the kingdom on his own and still sent Li Daliang with several thousand elite troops to support him.

sentences.zh: 順既久質於隋，國人不附，未幾為臣下所殺。

translations.literal: Since Shun had long been a hostage at Sui, the people did not attach themselves to him; before long he was killed by his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shun had spent so many years as a hostage at the Sui court, his people would not rally to him, and before long his own subordinates killed him.

sentences.zh: 其子燕王諾曷缽嗣立。

translations.literal: His son, Prince of Yan Nuohebo, succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: His son Nuohebo, Prince of Yan, succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 諾曷缽既幼，大臣爭權，國中大亂。

translations.literal: Nuohebo being young, ministers contested for power and the state fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Nuohebo was still young. Ministers fought for power, and the kingdom fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣兵援之，封為河源郡王。

translations.literal: Taizong sent troops to aid him and enfeoffed him as Prince of Heyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent troops to support him and enfeoffed him as Prince of Heyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 仍授烏地也拔勒豆可汗，遣淮陽王道明持節冊拜，賜以鼓纛。

translations.literal: He was further invested as Khan Wudiye Baledou; Prince Daoming of Huaiyang was dispatched with ceremonial credentials to confer the investiture, and drums and banners were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: He was also invested as Khan Wudiye Baledou. Prince Daoming of Huaiyang was sent with ceremonial credentials to confer the title, and drums and banners were granted.

sentences.zh: 諾曷缽因入朝請婚。

translations.literal: Nuohebo thereupon came to court to request a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Nuohebo then came to court to request a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 十四年，太宗以弘化公主妻之，資送甚厚。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Taizong gave him Princess Honghua in marriage with a very generous dowry.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, Taizong gave him Princess Honghua in marriage with a lavish dowry.

sentences.zh: 十五年，諾曷缽所部丞相王專權，陰謀作難。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, the Prime Minister Wang in Nuohebo's domain monopolized power and secretly plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, Prime Minister Wang in Nuohebo's domain seized power and secretly plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 將征兵，詐言祭山神，因欲襲擊公主，劫諾曷缽奔於吐蕃，期有日矣。

translations.literal: About to levy troops, he falsely claimed to sacrifice to the mountain god—his plan was to surprise and attack the princess, seize Nuohebo, and flee to Tibet; the day was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to levy troops, he claimed he was sacrificing to the mountain god, but in fact planned to surprise the princess, seize Nuohebo, and flee to Tibet. The day had already been set.

sentences.zh: 諾曷缽知而大懼，率輕騎走鄯善城，其威信王以兵迎之。

translations.literal: Nuohebo learned of it and was greatly afraid; leading light cavalry he fled to Shanshan City, and the Weixin King came with troops to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: When Nuohebo learned of the plot, he was terrified. He fled with a light escort to Shanshan City, where the Weixin King came out with troops to receive him.

sentences.zh: 鄯州刺史杜鳳舉與威信王合軍擊丞相王，破之，殺其兄弟三人，遣使言狀。

translations.literal: Shan Prefecture inspector Du Fengju joined forces with the Weixin King to attack Prime Minister Wang, defeated him, killed his three brothers, and sent envoys to report the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Du Fengju, inspector of Shan Prefecture, joined the Weixin King in attacking Prime Minister Wang, defeated him, killed his three brothers, and sent envoys to report what had happened.

sentences.zh: 太宗命民部尚書唐儉持節撫慰之。

translations.literal: Taizong ordered Minister of Revenue Tang Jian to proceed with ceremonial credentials to comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong ordered Tang Jian, Minister of Revenue, to proceed with ceremonial credentials and offer reassurance.

sentences.zh: 太宗崩，刻石圖諾曷缽之形，列於昭陵之下。

translations.literal: When Taizong died, a stone carving depicting Nuohebo's likeness was placed below Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong died, a stone carving of Nuohebo's likeness was placed below Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣位，以其尚主，拜駙馬都尉，賜物四十段。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded, because he had married a princess, he was appointed Commandant Escort and given forty rolls of goods.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, Nuohebo was made Commandant Escort because he had married an imperial princess, and was granted forty rolls of goods.

sentences.zh: 其後與吐蕃互相攻伐，各遣使請兵救援，高宗皆不許之。

translations.literal: Thereafter he and Tibet attacked each other in turn; each sent envoys requesting military aid, and Gaozong refused them all.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Tuyuhun and Tibet attacked each other in turn. Each side sent envoys asking for military aid, and Gaozong refused them all.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃大怒，率兵以擊吐谷渾。

translations.literal: Tibet was greatly angered and led troops to attack Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Tibet marched against Tuyuhun in force.

sentences.zh: 諾曷缽既不能禦，脫身及弘化公主走投涼州。

translations.literal: Nuohebo could not defend against them; he escaped with Princess Honghua and fled to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Nuohebo could not hold them off. He escaped with Princess Honghua and fled to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 高宗遣右威衛大將軍薛仁貴等救吐谷渾，為吐蕃所敗，於是吐谷渾遂為吐蕃所並。

translations.literal: Gaozong sent Right Weiw-wei Grand General Xue Rengui and others to rescue Tuyuhun; they were defeated by Tibet, and Tuyuhun was thereupon absorbed by Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong sent Xue Rengui, Grand General of the Right Weiw-wei Guard, and others to rescue Tuyuhun, but they were defeated by Tibet. Tuyuhun was then absorbed by Tibet.

sentences.zh: 諾曷缽以親信數千帳來內屬，詔左武衛大將軍蘇定方為安置大使，始徙其部眾於靈州之地，置安樂州，以諾曷缽為刺史，欲其安而且樂也。

translations.literal: Nuohebo came to submit with several thousand households of trusted followers; an edict appointed Left Wuwei Grand General Su Dingfang as Settlement Commissioner; they were first relocated to Lingzhou territory, establishing Anle Prefecture with Nuohebo as prefect—the name meant that he should be secure and content.
translations.idiomatic: Nuohebo came to submit with several thousand households of trusted followers. Su Dingfang, Grand General of the Left Wuwei Guard, was appointed Settlement Commissioner. His people were first moved to territory around Lingzhou, where Anle Prefecture was established with Nuohebo as prefect—a name chosen in the hope that he would live in security and contentment.

sentences.zh: 垂拱四年，諾曷缽卒，子忠嗣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chuigong, Nuohebo died; his son Zhong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chuigong, Nuohebo died and was succeeded by his son Zhong.

sentences.zh: 忠卒，子宣趙嗣。

translations.literal: Zhong died; his son Xuanzhao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong died and was succeeded by his son Xuanzhao.

sentences.zh: 聖歷三年，授宣趙左豹韜衛員外大將軍，仍襲父烏地也拔勒豆可汗。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shenglu, Xuanzhao was appointed Supernumerary Grand General of the Left Baotao Guard and also inherited his father's title Khan Wudiye Baledou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shenglu, Xuanzhao was made Supernumerary Grand General of the Left Baotao Guard and also inherited his father's title of Khan Wudiye Baledou.

sentences.zh: 宣趙卒，子曦皓嗣。

translations.literal: Xuanzhao died; his son Xihao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzhao died and was succeeded by his son Xihao.

sentences.zh: 曦皓卒，子兆嗣，及吐蕃陷我安樂州，其部眾又東徙，散在朔方、河東之境。

translations.literal: Xihao died; his son Zhao succeeded; when Tibet captured our Anle Prefecture, their tribesmen migrated east again, scattered across Shuofang and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xihao died and was succeeded by his son Zhao. When Tibet captured Anle Prefecture, the Tuyuhun tribes migrated east again and were scattered across Shuofang and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 今俗多謂之退渾，蓋語急而然。

translations.literal: Nowadays people commonly call them Tuihun—simply because the words are spoken quickly.
translations.idiomatic: People today commonly call them Tuihun—simply because the name is spoken quickly.

sentences.zh: 貞元十四年十二月，以朔方節度副使、左金吾衛大將軍同正慕容復為襲長樂州都督、青海國王、烏地也拔勒豆可汗。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan, Shuofang Deputy Military Commissioner and Left Jinwu Guard Grand General with Full Rank Murong Fu was invested to succeed as Protector-General of Changle Prefecture, King of Qinghai, and Khan Wudiye Baledou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan, Murong Fu—Deputy Military Commissioner of Shuofang and Left Jinwu Guard Grand General with Full Rank—was invested to succeed as Protector-General of Changle Prefecture, King of Qinghai, and Khan Wudiye Baledou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，其封襲遂絕。

translations.literal: Before long he died, and the enfeoffment and succession thereafter ended.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died, and the enfeoffment and succession came to an end.

sentences.zh: 葉谷渾自晉永嘉之末，始西渡洮水，建國於群羌之故地，至龍朔三年為吐蕃所滅，凡三百五十年。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun, from the end of the Yongjia era of Jin, first crossed west over the Tao River and established a state in the old lands of the Qiang tribes; until the third year of Longshuo they were destroyed by Tibet—in all three hundred and fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun, from the end of the Yongjia era of Jin, first crossed the Tao River westward and founded a state in the old lands of the Qiang tribes. They endured until the third year of Longshuo, when Tibet destroyed them—a span of three hundred and fifty years in all.

sentences.zh: 焉耆國

translations.literal: The Kingdom of Yanqi
translations.idiomatic: Yanqi

sentences.zh: 焉耆國，在京師西四千三百里，東接高昌，西鄰龜茲，即漢時故地。

translations.literal: The Kingdom of Yanqi is four thousand three hundred li west of the capital; east it adjoins Gaochang, west it neighbors Kucha—the territory of Han times.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Yanqi lay four thousand three hundred li west of the capital, bordering Gaochang to the east and Kucha to the west—the same territory known in Han times.

sentences.zh: 其王姓龍氏，名突騎支。

translations.literal: Its king was surnamed Long and named Tuqizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Its king bore the surname Long and was named Tuqizhi.

sentences.zh: 勝兵二千余人，常役屬於西突厥。

translations.literal: Fit for battle were more than two thousand soldiers; they were regularly subject to and dependent on the Western Turks.
translations.idiomatic: It could field more than two thousand fighting men and was regularly subject to the Western Turks.

sentences.zh: 其地良沃，多蒲萄，頗有魚鹽之利。

translations.literal: Its land was fertile and rich, with many grapes, and considerable profit from fish and salt.
translations.idiomatic: Its land was fertile and rich in grapes, and it enjoyed considerable profit from fish and salt.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年，突騎支遣使貢方物，復請開大磧路以便行李，太宗許之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan, Tuqizhi sent envoys presenting local products and again requested opening the Great Desert route to facilitate travel; Taizong granted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenguan, Tuqizhi sent envoys with local tribute and again asked that the Great Desert route be opened to ease travel. Taizong agreed.

sentences.zh: 自隋末罹亂，磧路遂閉，西域朝貢者皆由高昌。

translations.literal: Since the disorders at the end of Sui, the desert route had been closed, and Western Region tribute missions all went by way of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: Since the chaos at the end of the Sui, the desert route had been closed, and tribute missions from the Western Regions all went through Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 及是，高昌大怒，遂與焉耆結怨，遣兵襲焉耆，大掠而去。

translations.literal: At this, Gaochang was greatly angered, then formed enmity with Yanqi, sent troops to raid Yanqi, and departed after great plunder.
translations.idiomatic: At this Gaochang was furious. It turned against Yanqi, sent troops to raid the kingdom, and withdrew after a major plunder.

sentences.zh: 西突厥莫賀設與咄陸、弩失畢不協，奔於焉耆，咄陸復來攻之。

translations.literal: The Western Turk Mohe She was at odds with Duluo and the Nushibi; he fled to Yanqi, and Duluo came again to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe She of the Western Turks fell out with Duluo and the Nushibi, fled to Yanqi, and Duluo then attacked Yanqi again.

sentences.zh: 六年，遣使言狀，並貢名馬。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he sent envoys to report the situation and also presented famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Tuqizhi sent envoys to report what had happened and also presented fine horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 時西突厥國亂，太宗遣中郎將桑孝彥領左右胄曹韋弘機往安撫之，仍冊立咥利失可汗。

translations.literal: At that time the Western Turk state was in disorder; Taizong sent Central Commandant Sang Xiaoyan leading Left and Right Armorer Clerk Wei Hongji to pacify them, and also invested Xielishi as khan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Western Turk realm was in turmoil. Taizong sent Central Commandant Sang Xiaoyan with Armorer Clerk Wei Hongji of the Left and Right Bureaus to pacify them and invested Xielishi as khan.

sentences.zh: 可汗既立，素善焉耆，令與焉耆為援。

translations.literal: Once the khan was established, he had long been on good terms with Yanqi and ordered that Yanqi be given as support.
translations.idiomatic: Once the khan was established, he—who had long been friendly with Yanqi—ordered that Yanqi be supported as an ally.

sentences.zh: 十二年，處月、處密與高昌攻陷焉耆五城，掠男女一千五百人，焚其廬舍而去。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Chuyue, Chumi, and Gaochang attacked and captured five cities of Yanqi, carried off one thousand five hundred men and women, burned their dwellings, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, Chuyue and Chumi together with Gaochang captured five Yanqi cities, carried off fifteen hundred people, burned their dwellings, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十四年，侯君集討高昌，遣使與之相結，焉耆王大喜，請為聲援。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Hou Junji campaigned against Gaochang; he sent envoys to ally with Yanqi, and the Yanqi king was greatly pleased and asked to serve as backing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, as Hou Junji campaigned against Gaochang, he sent envoys to ally with Yanqi. The Yanqi king was delighted and offered to support him.

sentences.zh: 及破高昌，其王詣軍門稱謁。

translations.literal: When Gaochang was defeated, its king came to the army gate to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaochang fell, the Yanqi king came to the army camp to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 焉耆人先為高昌所虜者，悉歸之。

translations.literal: Yanqi people who had earlier been captured by Gaochang were all returned.
translations.idiomatic: All Yanqi people who had earlier been taken captive by Gaochang were returned.

sentences.zh: 由是遣使謝恩，並貢方物。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent envoys to express gratitude and also presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Tuqizhi sent envoys to express gratitude and also presented local tribute.

sentences.zh: 其年，西突厥重臣屈利啜為其弟娶焉耆王女，由是相為脣齒，朝貢遂闕。

translations.literal: That year, the Western Turk senior minister Qulichuo had his younger brother marry the Yanqi king's daughter; thereby they became mutually dependent like lips and teeth, and tribute missions thereafter ceased.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Western Turk senior minister Qulichuo had his younger brother marry the Yanqi king's daughter. The two sides became close as lips and teeth, and Yanqi's tribute missions ceased.

sentences.zh: 安西都護郭孝恪請擊之，太宗許焉。

translations.literal: Protector-General of Anxi Guo Xiaoke requested to attack them; Taizong granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiaoke, Protector-General of Anxi, asked permission to attack Yanqi, and Taizong agreed.

sentences.zh: 會焉耆王弟頡鼻葉護兄弟三人來至西州，孝恪選步騎三千出銀山道，以頡鼻弟栗婆準為鄉導。

translations.literal: It happened that the Yanqi king's younger brother Xieni Yehu and his three brothers came to Xizhou; Xiaoke selected three thousand infantry and cavalry to set out by the Yinshan route, with Xieni's younger brother Lipozhun as guide.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the Yanqi king's younger brother Xieni Yehu and his three brothers came to Xizhou. Xiaoke chose three thousand infantry and cavalry to march out by the Yinshan route, with Xieni's younger brother Lipozhun as guide.

sentences.zh: 焉耆所都城，四面有水，自恃險固，不虞於我。

translations.literal: The city where Yanqi was based had water on all four sides; relying on its perilous strength, it did not expect attack from our forces.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqi's capital was surrounded by water on all four sides. Trusting in its natural defenses, it did not expect an attack from the Tang.

sentences.zh: 孝恪倍道兼行，夜至城下，潛遣將士浮水而渡。

translations.literal: Xiaoke marched at double speed day and night, arrived at the city by night, and secretly sent officers and soldiers to float across the water and cross.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoke forced the march day and night, reached the city after dark, and secretly sent his men across the water.

sentences.zh: 至曉，一時攀堞，鼓角齊震，城中大擾。

translations.literal: By dawn they all climbed the battlements at once; drums and horns sounded together, and great disorder arose in the city.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they scaled the walls all at once. Drums and horns sounded together, and the city erupted in chaos.

sentences.zh: 孝恪縱兵擊之，虜其王突騎支，首虜千余級。

translations.literal: Xiaoke unleashed his troops to attack them, captured their king Tuqizhi, and took more than a thousand heads and captives.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoke unleashed his troops, captured King Tuqizhi, and took more than a thousand heads and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 以栗婆準導軍有功，留攝國事而還。

translations.literal: Because Lipozhun had merit in guiding the army, he was left to administer state affairs and Xiaoke returned.
translations.idiomatic: Because Lipozhun had guided the army well, Xiaoke left him in charge of state affairs and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時駕幸洛陽宮，孝恪鎖突騎支並其妻子送行在所，詔宥之。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was visiting Luoyang Palace; Xiaoke fettered Tuqizhi together with his wife and children and sent them to the traveling residence; an edict pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then at Luoyang Palace. Xiaoke sent Tuqizhi in chains, together with his wife and children, to the imperial residence, and an edict pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 初，西突厥屈利啜將兵來援焉耆，孝恪還師三日，屈利啜乃囚栗婆準，而西突厥處般啜令其吐屯來攝焉耆，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Initially, the Western Turk Qulichuo led troops to aid Yanqi; three days after Xiaoke withdrew his army, Qulichuo then imprisoned Lipozhun, while the Western Turk Chubanchuo ordered his tutun to come and administer Yanqi and sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Qulichuo of the Western Turks had marched to aid Yanqi. Three days after Xiaoke withdrew, Qulichuo imprisoned Lipozhun. Chubanchuo of the Western Turks then sent his tutun to take control of Yanqi and dispatched envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 太宗數之曰：「焉耆者，我兵擊得，汝何人，輒來統攝。」

translations.literal: Taizong rebuked him, saying: "Yanqi was taken by Our army—who are you to come and administer it?
translations.idiomatic: Taizong rebuked him, saying, "Yanqi was taken by our armies—who are you to come and rule it?

sentences.zh: 吐屯懼而返國。

translations.literal: The tutun, afraid, returned to his state.
translations.idiomatic: The tutun, terrified, returned home.

sentences.zh: 焉耆又立栗婆準從父兄薛婆阿那支為王。

translations.literal: Yanqi again enthroned Lipozhun's father's elder brother's son Xiepo Anazhi as king.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqi then enthroned Lipozhun's cousin Xiepo Anazhi as king.

sentences.zh: 處般啜乃執栗婆準送於龜茲，為所殺。

translations.literal: Chubanchuo then seized Lipozhun and sent him to Kucha, where he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Chubanchuo seized Lipozhun and sent him to Kucha, where he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 薛婆阿那支既得處般啜為援，遂有國。

translations.literal: Xiepo Anazhi, having obtained Chubanchuo as support, then held the state.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiepo Anazhi gained Chubanchuo as an ally, he secured control of the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 及阿史那社爾之討龜茲，阿那支大懼，遂奔龜茲，保其東城，以禦官軍。

translations.literal: When Ashina She'er campaigned against Kucha, Anazhi was greatly afraid, fled to Kucha, and held its eastern city to oppose the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: When Ashina She'er marched against Kucha, Anazhi was terrified. He fled to Kucha and defended its eastern city against the Tang forces.

sentences.zh: 社爾擊擒之，數其罪而斬焉。

translations.literal: She'er attacked, captured him, reckoned his crimes, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: She'er captured him, enumerated his crimes, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 求得阿那支從父弟先那準，立為王，以修職貢。

translations.literal: He sought and found Anazhi's father's younger brother's son Xiannazhun, enthroned him as king, and had him restore official tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He found Anazhi's cousin Xiannazhun, installed him as king, and restored Yanqi's tribute obligations.

sentences.zh: 及太宗葬昭陵。

translations.literal: When Taizong was buried at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong was interred at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 乃刻石像龍突騎支之形，列於玄闕之下。

translations.literal: Thereupon a stone image of Long Tuoqizhi's form was carved and arrayed below the Spirit Gate.
translations.idiomatic: A stone likeness of Long Tuoqizhi was carved and placed before the Spirit Gate of the tomb.

sentences.zh: 自是朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: From this time tribute missions were unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute missions thereafter never ceased.

sentences.zh: 龜茲國，即漢西域舊地也。

translations.literal: The Kingdom of Kucha is the old territory of the Western Regions in Han times.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Kucha occupied the same lands known as the Western Regions in Han times.

sentences.zh: 在京師西七千五百里。

translations.literal: It is seven thousand five hundred li west of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: It lay seven thousand five hundred li west of the capital.

sentences.zh: 其王姓白氏。

translations.literal: Its kings bear the surname Bai.
translations.idiomatic: The royal house bore the surname Bai.

sentences.zh: 有城郭屋宇，耕田畜牧為業。

translations.literal: They have walled cities and houses; farming and herding are their occupation.
translations.idiomatic: The people lived in walled towns and houses, earning their livelihood by farming and raising livestock.

sentences.zh: 男女皆翦髮，垂與項齊，唯王不翦髮。

translations.literal: Men and women all cut their hair short so that it hangs level with the nape; only the king does not cut his hair.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women alike cropped their hair to hang level with the nape of the neck; only the king wore his hair long.

sentences.zh: 學胡書及婆羅門書、算計之事，尤重佛法。

translations.literal: They study foreign script and Brahmin script and matters of calculation; they especially esteem the Buddhist Law.
translations.idiomatic: They studied foreign scripts and Brahmi writing, as well as arithmetic; above all they revered Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 其王以錦蒙項，著錦袍金寶帶，坐金獅子床。

translations.literal: The king covers his neck with brocade, wears a brocade robe and a gold jeweled belt, and sits on a golden lion couch.
translations.idiomatic: The king draped brocade over his neck, wore a brocade robe with a jeweled gold belt, and sat upon a golden lion throne.

sentences.zh: 有良馬、封牛。

translations.literal: They have fine horses and humped cattle.
translations.idiomatic: The country produced fine horses and zebu cattle.

sentences.zh: 饒蒲萄酒，富室至數百碩。

translations.literal: Grape wine is abundant; wealthy households keep as much as several hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: Grape wine was plentiful; affluent families stored several hundred shi of it.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，其主蘇伐勃駃遣使來朝。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, its ruler Suwafu dispatched envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, the Kuchan ruler Suwafu sent envoys to pay court.

sentences.zh: 勃駃尋卒，子蘇伐疊代立，號時健莫賀俟利發。

translations.literal: Fu soon died; his son Suwafdie succeeded, styled Shijian Mohe Shilifa.
translations.idiomatic: Suwafu died soon afterward. His son Suwafdie succeeded him, taking the title Shijian Mohe Shilifa.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年，又遣使獻馬，太宗賜以璽書，撫慰甚厚，由此歲貢不絕，然臣於西突厥。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan, envoys were again sent presenting horses; Taizong bestowed an imperial edict and treated them with great kindness. Thereafter annual tribute was unceasing, yet they were subject to the Western Turks.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Zhenguan reign, Kucha again sent horses as tribute. Taizong responded with an imperial letter of reassurance and lavish kindness. Annual tribute thereafter continued without interruption, though the kingdom remained subject to the Western Turks.

sentences.zh: 安西都護郭孝恪來伐焉耆，龜茲遣兵援助，自是職貢頗闕。

translations.literal: Protector-General of Anxi Guo Xiaoke came to attack Yanqi; Kucha sent troops in aid, and from this time official tribute was largely lacking.
translations.idiomatic: When Protector-General Guo Xiaoke of Anxi marched against Yanqi, Kucha sent troops to aid it. Official tribute to the Tang thereafter largely ceased.

sentences.zh: 伐疊死，其弟訶黎布失畢代立，漸失籓臣禮。

translations.literal: Fadie died; his younger brother Helibushi succeeded and gradually lost the proprieties of a vassal.
translations.idiomatic: When Suwafdie died, his younger brother Helibushi succeeded him and gradually abandoned the manners due a vassal state.

sentences.zh: 二十年，太宗遣左驍衛大將軍阿史那社爾為昆山道行軍大總管，與安西都護郭孝恪、司農卿楊弘禮率五將軍，又發鐵勒十三部兵十余萬騎，以伐龜茲。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Taizong dispatched Left Xiaoqiwei Grand General Ashina She'er as Grand Commander of the Kunshan Route Army, who together with Protector-General of Anxi Guo Xiaoke and Minister of Public Works Yang Hongli led five generals, and also mobilized more than one hundred thousand cavalry from the thirteen Tiele tribes, to attack Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, Taizong appointed Left Xiaoqiwei Grand General Ashina She'er commander of the Kunshan Route campaign. Together with Protector-General Guo Xiaoke of Anxi and Minister of Public Works Yang Hongli, he led five generals and mustered more than one hundred thousand cavalry from the thirteen Tiele tribes to invade Kucha.

sentences.zh: 社爾既破西蕃處月、處密，乃進師趨其北境，出其不意，西突厥所署焉耆王棄城而遁，社爾遣輕騎追擒之。

translations.literal: She'er having already defeated the Western tribes Chuyue and Chumi, then advanced his army toward Kucha's northern border, catching them unprepared; the Yanqi king installed by the Western Turks abandoned the city and fled; She'er sent light cavalry in pursuit and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating the Chuyue and Chumi tribes in the west, She'er marched on Kucha's northern frontier by surprise. The Yanqi king appointed by the Western Turks abandoned his city and fled, but She'er's light cavalry pursued and captured him.

sentences.zh: 龜茲大震，守將多棄城而走。

translations.literal: Kucha was greatly shaken; many defending generals abandoned their cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Kucha was thrown into panic, and many garrison commanders abandoned their cities and fled.

sentences.zh: 社爾進屯積石，去其都城三百里。

translations.literal: She'er advanced and encamped at Jishi, three hundred li from the capital city.
translations.idiomatic: She'er advanced and encamped at Jishi, three hundred li from the Kuchan capital.

sentences.zh: 遣伊州刺史韓威率千余騎為前鋒，右驍衛將軍曹繼叔次之。

translations.literal: He dispatched Yizhou prefect Han Wei to lead more than a thousand cavalry as vanguard; Right Xiaoqiwei General Cao Jishu followed next.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yizhou prefect Han Wei ahead with more than a thousand cavalry as vanguard, with Right Xiaoqiwei General Cao Jishu following in support.

sentences.zh: 西至多褐城，與龜茲王相遇，及其相那利、將羯獵顛等，有眾五萬，逆拒王師。

translations.literal: Marching west to Duohe City, they encountered the Kuchan king together with his minister Nali, general Jieliedian, and others—fifty thousand in all—who opposed the imperial army head-on.
translations.idiomatic: West of Duohe City they met the Kuchan king, his minister Nali, General Jieliedian, and others at the head of fifty thousand men, who marched out to oppose the Tang army.

sentences.zh: 威乃偽遁而引之，其王俟利發見威兵少，悉眾而至。

translations.literal: Wei then feigned retreat to lure them; the king Shilifa, seeing Wei's troops were few, came with his entire force.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wei feigned a retreat to draw them in. King Shilifa, seeing how few Tang horsemen faced him, marched out with his entire army.

sentences.zh: 威退行三十里，與繼叔軍會，合擊大破之。

translations.literal: Wei withdrew thirty li and joined Cao Jishu's army; together they struck and utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wei fell back thirty li, linked up with Cao Jishu's force, and together they delivered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 其王退保都城，社爾進軍逼之，王乃輕騎而走，遂下其城，令孝恪守之。

translations.literal: The king withdrew to hold the capital city; She'er advanced and pressed him; the king then fled with light cavalry; they took the city and had Xiaoke hold it.
translations.idiomatic: The king retreated to defend his capital. She'er pressed the siege, and the king fled with a small cavalry escort. The Tang forces then took the city and left Guo Xiaoke to hold it.

sentences.zh: 遣沙州刺史蘇海政、尚輦奉禦薛萬備以精騎逼之，行六百里，其王窘急，退保於撥換城。

translations.literal: He dispatched Shazhou prefect Su Haizheng and Palace Steeds Attendant Xue Wanbei with elite cavalry to press him; after marching six hundred li, the king, hard pressed, withdrew to hold Bolanhuan City.
translations.idiomatic: She'er sent Shazhou prefect Su Haizheng and Palace Steeds Attendant Xue Wanbei after him with elite cavalry. After a pursuit of six hundred li, the beleaguered king took refuge in Bolanhuan.

sentences.zh: 社爾等進軍圍之，擒其王及大將羯獵顛等。

translations.literal: She'er and the others advanced, besieged it, and captured the king and Grand General Jieliedian and others.
translations.idiomatic: She'er and his officers besieged the city and captured the king and General Jieliedian along with his officers.

sentences.zh: 其相那利僅以身免，潛引西突厥之眾並其國兵萬余人，來襲孝恪，殺之，官軍大擾。

translations.literal: His minister Nali alone escaped with his body; secretly he led Western Turk forces together with more than ten thousand of the state's troops to raid Xiaoke, killed him, and the imperial army was greatly thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Nali alone escaped. Secretly rallying Western Turk allies and more than ten thousand Kuchan troops, he launched a surprise attack on Guo Xiaoke and killed him, throwing the Tang army into chaos.

sentences.zh: 倉部郎中崔義起與曹繼叔、韓威等擊之，那利敗走。

translations.literal: Bureau of Granaries director Cui Yiqi together with Cao Jishu, Han Wei, and others attacked; Nali was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yiqi of the Bureau of Granaries, together with Cao Jishu, Han Wei, and others, counterattacked and drove Nali into flight.

sentences.zh: 尋為龜茲人所執以詣軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was seized by men of Kucha and brought to the army.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon seized by Kuchans and delivered to the Tang camp.

sentences.zh: 前後破其大城五所，虜男女數萬口。

translations.literal: In all they broke five of its great cities and captured men and women numbering tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign they captured five major cities and took tens of thousands of men and women captive.

sentences.zh: 社爾因立其王之弟葉護為王，勒石紀功而旋。

translations.literal: She'er thereupon enthroned the king's younger brother Yehu as king, carved stone to record the achievement, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: She'er installed the king's younger brother Yehu on the throne, erected a stone monument to commemorate the victory, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 俘其王訶黎布失畢及那利、羯獵顛等獻於社廟。

translations.literal: The captives—the king Helibushi together with Nali, Jieliedian, and others—were presented at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: The captives—King Helibushi, Nali, Jieliedian, and the rest—were presented at the imperial ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 尋以訶黎布失畢為左武翊衛中郎將，那利已下授官各有差。

translations.literal: Soon Helibushi was made Left Wuyiwei Commandant of the Third Rank; Nali and those below were granted offices each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Helibushi was soon appointed Commandant of the Third Rank in the Left Wuyiwei Guard; Nali and the others received offices of varying rank.

sentences.zh: 太宗之葬昭陵，乃刻石像其形，列於玄闕之前。

translations.literal: At Taizong's burial at Zhaoling, a stone image of their forms was carved and arrayed before the Spirit Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong was buried at Zhaoling, stone likenesses of the captives were carved and set before the Spirit Gate.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年，又以訶黎布失畢為右驍衛大將軍，尋放還蕃，撫其余眾，依舊為龜茲王，賜物一千段。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui, Helibushi was again made Right Xiaoqiwei Grand General; soon he was released to return to his frontier land, soothed the remaining multitude, and continued as before as king of Kucha; one thousand bolts of goods were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yonghui reign, Helibushi was again appointed Right Xiaoqiwei Grand General. He was soon sent back to his homeland to reassure his remaining followers and resume his rule as king of Kucha, and was granted one thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 先是，太宗既破龜茲，移置安西都護府於其國城，以郭孝恪為都護，兼統於闐、疏勒、碎葉，謂之「四鎮」。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Taizong had defeated Kucha, the Protectorate General of Anxi was moved and established in its capital city, with Guo Xiaoke as Protector-General, also commanding Khotan, Kashgar, and Suyab—called the "Four Garrisons."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Taizong's conquest of Kucha, the Protectorate General of Anxi was relocated to the Kuchan capital. Guo Xiaoke served as Protector-General, with authority over Khotan, Kashgar, and Suyab as well—the so-called Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣位，不欲廣地勞人，復命有司棄龜茲等四鎮，移安西依舊於西州。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded the throne, not wishing to extend territory and weary the people, he again ordered the responsible offices to abandon Kucha and the other Four Garrisons and move Anxi back as before to Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong succeeded to the throne, unwilling to overextend the realm and exhaust the people, he ordered the Four Garrisons including Kucha abandoned and the Anxi Protectorate moved back to Xizhou as before.

sentences.zh: 其後吐蕃大入，焉耆已西四鎮城堡，並為賊所陷。

translations.literal: Afterward the Tibetans invaded on a great scale; the Four Garrisons' fortresses from Yanqi westward were all lost to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet later invaded in force, and the fortresses of the Four Garrisons west of Yanqi all fell to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，長壽元年，武威軍總管王孝傑、阿史那忠節大破吐蕃，克復龜茲、於闐等四鎮，自此復於龜茲置安西都護府，用漢兵三萬人以鎮之。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu held court, in the first year of Changshou, Commander of the Wuwei Army Wang Xiaojie and Ashina Zhongjie utterly defeated the Tibetans, recovered Kucha, Khotan, and the other Four Garrisons, and from this time again established the Protectorate General of Anxi at Kucha, employing thirty thousand Han troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Wu assumed power, Wang Xiaojie, commander of the Wuwei Army, and Ashina Zhongjie routed the Tibetans in the first year of Changshou and recaptured the Four Garrisons, including Kucha and Khotan. The Anxi Protectorate was then reestablished at Kucha, garrisoned by thirty thousand Han soldiers.

sentences.zh: 既征發內地精兵，遠逾沙磧。

translations.literal: Having mobilized elite troops from the interior, they crossed far beyond the sandy deserts.
translations.idiomatic: Elite troops were conscripted from the interior and marched far across the desert wastes.

sentences.zh: 並資遣衣糧等，甚為百姓所苦。

translations.literal: Together with provisions of clothing and grain sent forth, this was greatly painful to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: The provisioning of clothing and grain for these deployments inflicted severe hardship on the people.

sentences.zh: 言事者多請棄之，則天竟不許。

translations.literal: Many who spoke on affairs petitioned to abandon them; Empress Wu in the end did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Many memorialists urged abandoning the garrisons, but Empress Wu refused.

sentences.zh: 其安西都護，則天時有田揚名，中宗時有郭元振，開元初則張孝暠、杜暹，皆有政績，為夷人所伏。

translations.literal: Among the Protectors-General of Anxi: in Empress Wu's time there was Tian Yangming; in Zhongzong's time Guo Yuanzhen; at the beginning of Kaiyuan, Zhang Xiaohao and Du Xian—all had administrative achievements and were respected by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The Anxi Protectors-General included Tian Yangming under Empress Wu, Guo Yuanzhen under Emperor Zhongzong, and early in the Kaiyuan era Zhang Xiaohao and Du Xian—all men of proven achievement whom the frontier peoples respected.

sentences.zh: 疏勒國

translations.literal: The Kingdom of Kashgar
translations.idiomatic: Kashgar

sentences.zh: 疏勒國，即漢時舊地也。

translations.literal: The Kingdom of Kashgar is the old territory of Han times.
translations.idiomatic: Kashgar occupied territory known in Han times.

sentences.zh: 西帶蔥嶺，在京師西九千三百里。

translations.literal: West it borders the Pamirs; it is nine thousand three hundred li west of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: It bordered the Pamirs to the west and lay nine thousand three hundred li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 其王姓裴氏。

translations.literal: Its kings bear the surname Pei.
translations.idiomatic: The royal house bore the surname Pei.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，突厥以女妻王。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan, the Turks gave a daughter in marriage to the king.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign, the Turks gave a princess in marriage to the Kashgar king.

sentences.zh: 勝兵二千人。

translations.literal: Effective troops: two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: It could field two thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 俗事祅神，有胡書文字。

translations.literal: Their custom is to serve the Zoroastrian god; they have foreign script and writing.
translations.idiomatic: The people worshipped the Zoroastrian fire god and used a foreign script.

sentences.zh: 貞觀九年，遣使獻名馬，自是朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenguan, envoys were sent presenting famed horses; from this time tribute missions were unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhenguan it sent famed horses as tribute, and tribute missions thereafter continued without interruption.

sentences.zh: 開元十六年，玄宗遣使冊立其王裴安定為疏勒王。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan, Xuanzong dispatched envoys to invest its king Pei Anding as King of Kashgar.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan, Emperor Xuanzong sent envoys to invest Pei Anding as king of Kashgar.

sentences.zh: 於闐國

translations.literal: The Kingdom of Khotan
translations.idiomatic: Khotan

sentences.zh: 於闐國，西南帶蔥嶺，與龜茲接，在京師西九千七百里。

translations.literal: The Kingdom of Khotan borders the Pamirs to the southwest, adjoins Kucha, and is nine thousand seven hundred li west of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Khotan bordered the Pamirs to the southwest, adjoined Kucha, and lay nine thousand seven hundred li west of the capital.

sentences.zh: 勝兵四千人。

translations.literal: Effective troops: four thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: It could field four thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 其國出美玉。

translations.literal: The state produces fine jade.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom was famed for its fine jade.

sentences.zh: 俗多機巧，好事祅神，崇佛教。

translations.literal: Their customs have much ingenuity; they delight in serving the Zoroastrian god and revere the Buddhist Law.
translations.idiomatic: The people were ingenious by nature, honored the Zoroastrian cult, and also fervently embraced Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 先臣於西突厥。

translations.literal: Formerly they were subject to the Western Turks.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom had formerly been subject to the Western Turks.

sentences.zh: 其王姓尉遲氏，名屈密。

translations.literal: Its king bears the surname Yuchi, personal name Qumi.
translations.idiomatic: The king belonged to the Yuchi clan and was named Qumi.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年，遣使獻玉帶，太宗優詔答之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan, envoys were sent presenting a jade belt; Taizong responded with a gracious edict.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenguan it sent a jade belt as tribute, and Taizong replied with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 十三年，又遣子入侍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, a son was again sent to serve at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the king sent his son to serve at the Tang court.

sentences.zh: 及阿史那社爾伐龜茲，其王伏阇信大懼，使其子以駝萬三百匹饋軍。

translations.literal: When Ashina She'er attacked Kucha, its king Fuxinxin was greatly afraid and had his son present one thousand three hundred camels to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Ashina She'er invaded Kucha, King Fuxinxin was terrified and sent his son with thirteen hundred camels as a gift to the Tang army.

sentences.zh: 及將旋師，行軍長史薛萬備請社爾曰：「今者既破龜茲，國威已振，請因此機，願以輕騎羈取於闐之王。」

translations.literal: As they were about to withdraw the army, campaign chief administrator Xue Wanbei requested of She'er, saying: "Now that Kucha has been broken, our state's prestige is already shaken forth—please seize this opportunity; I wish to take the king of Khotan with light cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: As the army prepared to withdraw, campaign chief administrator Xue Wanbei proposed to She'er: "Now that Kucha has fallen and our prestige stands high, I ask that we seize this moment and take the king of Khotan with a detachment of light cavalry.

sentences.zh: 社爾乃遣萬備率五十騎抵於闐之國，萬備陳國威靈，勸其入見天子，伏阇信於是隨萬備來朝。

translations.literal: She'er then dispatched Wanbei to lead fifty horsemen to arrive at the state of Khotan; Wanbei set forth the state's awesome numen and urged him to come in person to see the Son of Heaven; Fuxinxin thereupon followed Wanbei to court.
translations.idiomatic: She'er sent Xue Wanbei with fifty horsemen to Khotan. Xue Wanbei proclaimed the Tang dynasty's majesty and urged the king to come pay homage to the Son of Heaven. Fuxinxin accordingly accompanied him to court.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣位，拜右驍衛大將軍，又授其子葉護玷為右驍衛將軍，並賜金帶、錦袍、布帛六十段，並宅一區，留數月而遣之，因請留子弟以宿衛。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded the throne, he appointed Fuxinxin Right Xiaoqiwei Grand General, also granted his son Yehu Dian as Right Xiaoqiwei General, and together bestowed a gold belt, brocade robe, sixty bolts of cloth and silk, and one residence; after retaining him several months he sent him away; he thereupon requested to leave younger kinsmen to serve as inner guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong succeeded to the throne, he appointed Fuxinxin Right Xiaoqiwei Grand General and his son Yehu Dian Right Xiaoqiwei General, granting them gold belts, brocade robes, sixty bolts of silk, and a residence in the capital. After several months at court Fuxinxin was sent home, having asked to leave younger relatives behind as palace guards.

sentences.zh: 太宗葬昭陵，刻石像其形，列於玄闕之下。

translations.literal: At Taizong's burial at Zhaoling, a stone image of his form was carved and arrayed below the Spirit Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong was buried at Zhaoling, a stone likeness of Fuxinxin was carved and placed before the Spirit Gate.

sentences.zh: 垂拱三年，其王伏阇雄復來入朝。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chuigong, its king Fuhu Xiong again came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Chuigong reign, King Fuhu Xiong again came to pay court.

sentences.zh: 天授三年，伏阇雄卒，則天封其子璥為於闐國王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianshou, Fuhu Xiong died; Empress Wu enfeoffed his son Jin as King of Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: Fuhu Xiong died in the third year of Tianshou, and Empress Wu enfeoffed his son Jin as king of Khotan.

sentences.zh: 開元十六年，復冊立尉遲伏師為於闐王，數遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan, Yuchi Fushi was again invested as King of Khotan; envoys were repeatedly sent with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan, Yuchi Fushi was again invested as king of Khotan, and tribute missions followed in number.

sentences.zh: 乾元三年，以於闐王尉遲勝弟守左監門衛率葉護曜為太仆員外卿，仍同四鎮節度副使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianyuan, the Khotan king Yuchi Sheng's younger brother, Commandant of the Left Gate Guard Yehu Yao, was made Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud without full rank, and also Associate Deputy Commissioner of the Four Garrisons Command.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qianyuan, Yehu Yao—the younger brother of Khotan king Yuchi Sheng and Commandant of the Left Gate Guard—was appointed Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud and named deputy commissioner of the Four Garrisons command.

sentences.zh: 權知本國事。

translations.literal: He was empowered provisionally to administer the affairs of his native state.
translations.idiomatic: He was authorized to govern Khotan on a provisional basis.

sentences.zh: 以勝至德初領兵赴國難，因堅請留宿衛，故有是命，事有勝傳。

translations.literal: Because Sheng at the beginning of Zhide led troops to respond to the state's crisis and therefore firmly requested to remain as inner guard, there was this appointment; the affair is recorded in Sheng's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yuchi Sheng had marched to the capital's aid at the start of the Zhide reign and insisted on remaining as a palace guard, this appointment was made; the fuller account appears in his biography.

sentences.zh: 天竺國

translations.literal: The Kingdom of India
translations.idiomatic: India

sentences.zh: 天竺國，即漢之身毒國，或云婆羅門地也。

translations.literal: The Kingdom of India is Han's Shendu Kingdom, or it is said to be the land of the Brahmins.
translations.idiomatic: India was known in Han times as Shendu—the land of the Brahmins, as some accounts have it.

sentences.zh: 在蔥嶺西北，周三萬餘里。

translations.literal: It lies northwest of the Pamirs; its circumference is more than thirty thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: It lay northwest of the Pamirs and measured more than thirty thousand li in circumference.

sentences.zh: 其中分為五天竺：其一曰中天竺，二曰東天竺，三曰南天竺，四曰西天竺，五曰北天竺。

translations.literal: Within it India is divided into five Indias: the first is Middle India, the second East India, the third South India, the fourth West India, the fifth North India.
translations.idiomatic: The subcontinent was divided into five Indias: Middle, East, South, West, and North.

sentences.zh: 地各數千里，城邑數百。

translations.literal: Each territory is several thousand li; there are several hundred cities and towns.
translations.idiomatic: Each region spanned several thousand li and contained hundreds of towns and cities.

sentences.zh: 南天竺際大海，北天竺拒雪山，四周有山為壁，南面一谷，通為國門；

translations.literal: South India borders the great sea; North India faces the Snow Mountains; on all four sides mountains form walls; one valley to the south serves as the gate of the state;
translations.idiomatic: South India bordered the ocean; North India abutted the Snow Mountains. Mountains walled it on every side, with a single southern valley serving as the nation's gateway;

sentences.zh: 東天竺東際大海，與扶南、林邑鄰接；

translations.literal: East India to the east borders the great sea and adjoins Funan and Linyi;
translations.idiomatic: East India faced the eastern sea and bordered Funan and Linyi;

sentences.zh: 西天竺與罽賓、波斯相接；

translations.literal: West India connects with Kapisa and Persia;
translations.idiomatic: West India adjoined Kapisa and Persia;

sentences.zh: 中天竺據四天竺之會，其都城周回七十餘里，北臨禪連河。

translations.literal: Middle India occupies the meeting point of the four Indias; its capital city has a circumference of more than seventy li and faces the Chanlian River to the north.
translations.idiomatic: Middle India stood at the heart of the four regions. Its capital measured more than seventy li in circumference and looked north upon the Chanlian River—the Ganges.

sentences.zh: 云昔有婆羅門領徒千人，肄業於樹下，樹神降之，遂為夫婦。

translations.literal: It is said that long ago a Brahmin led a thousand disciples to study under a tree; the tree spirit descended to him, and they became husband and wife.
translations.idiomatic: Legend holds that a Brahmin once led a thousand disciples in study beneath a sacred tree. The tree spirit descended and took him as her husband.

sentences.zh: 宮室自然而立，僮仆甚盛。

translations.literal: Palace halls arose of themselves; servants were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Palaces sprang up as if of their own accord, attended by a vast host of servants.

sentences.zh: 於是使役百神，築城以統之，經日而就。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made the hundred spirits serve him, built a city to rule them, and it was completed within a day.
translations.idiomatic: He then commanded the hundred spirits and built a city to rule over them—a task completed in a single day.

sentences.zh: 此後有阿育王，復役使鬼神，累石為宮闕，皆雕文刻鏤。

translations.literal: After this there was King Ashoka, who again conscripted ghosts and spirits; piling stone for palace towers, all were carved with patterns and inlaid with cut ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Later came King Ashoka, who likewise pressed ghosts and spirits into service, stacking stone into palaces adorned with elaborate carving and inlay.

sentences.zh: 非人力所及。

translations.literal: It is not within the reach of human power.
translations.idiomatic: Such works lay beyond human capacity.

sentences.zh: 阿育王頗行茍政，置砲烙之刑，謂之地獄，今城中見有其跡焉。

translations.literal: King Ashoka frequently practiced harsh government, establishing the branding-pillar punishment, called "Hell"; traces of it can still be seen in the city today.
translations.idiomatic: Ashoka ruled harshly, instituting a branding-pillar torture he called "Hell"—traces of which can still be seen in the city.

sentences.zh: 中天竺王姓乞利咥氏，或云剎利氏，世有其國，不相篡弒。

translations.literal: The kings of Middle India bear the surname Qilidie, or it is said the Kshatriya clan; they hold their state generation after generation without usurping or assassinating one another.
translations.idiomatic: Middle India's kings belonged to the Qilidie clan—or the Kshatriya, as some say—and held the throne by hereditary succession without usurpation or regicide.

sentences.zh: 厥土卑濕暑熱，稻歲四熟，有金剛，似紫石英，百煉不銷，可以切玉。

translations.literal: Its soil is low, damp, hot and humid; rice ripens four times a year; there is diamond, resembling amethyst, which even after a hundred refinings does not wear away and can cut jade.
translations.idiomatic: The land was low, humid, and sweltering; rice yielded four harvests a year. There was diamond—hard as amethyst, indestructible even after repeated firing—that could slice through jade.

sentences.zh: 又有旃檀、郁金諸香。

translations.literal: There are also sandalwood, turmeric, and various fragrances.
translations.idiomatic: Sandalwood, turmeric, and other aromatics grew there as well.

sentences.zh: 通於大秦，故其寶物或至扶南、交趾貿易焉。

translations.literal: It connects with Daqin; therefore its precious goods sometimes reach Funan and Jiaozhi for trade.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom had contact with Rome, and its treasures were traded as far as Funan and Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 百姓殷樂，俗無簿籍，耕王地者輸地利。

translations.literal: The common people are prosperous and content; the custom has no registers; those who cultivate the king's land render land profit.
translations.idiomatic: The people were prosperous and untroubled. No land registry was kept; farmers working royal lands paid a share of the produce.

sentences.zh: 以齒貝為貨。

translations.literal: Cowrie shells serve as currency.
translations.idiomatic: Cowrie shells served as currency.

sentences.zh: 人皆深目長鼻。

translations.literal: The people all have deep-set eyes and long noses.
translations.idiomatic: The people had deep-set eyes and prominent noses.

sentences.zh: 致敬極者，舐足摩踵。

translations.literal: Those who show the utmost respect lick the feet and rub the heels.
translations.idiomatic: The deepest obeisance was paid by licking the feet and massaging the heels.

sentences.zh: 家有奇樂倡伎。

translations.literal: Households keep marvelous music and singing girls.
translations.idiomatic: Well-to-do households maintained fine music and courtesans.

sentences.zh: 其王與大臣多服錦罽。

translations.literal: Its king and great ministers mostly wear brocade and felt rugs.
translations.idiomatic: The king and his chief ministers commonly wore brocade and felted wool.

sentences.zh: 上為螺髻於頂，餘髮翦之使拳。

translations.literal: On top they form a spiral topknot; the remaining hair is cut short and curled into fists.
translations.idiomatic: Men wore a coiled topknot on the crown and cropped the rest of the hair into tight curls.

sentences.zh: 俗皆徒跣。

translations.literal: The custom is all to go barefoot.
translations.idiomatic: Going barefoot was the universal custom.

sentences.zh: 衣重白色，唯梵誌種姓披白疊以為異。

translations.literal: Clothing favors white; only the Brahmin caste wears white layered cloth as a distinction.
translations.idiomatic: White was the favored color of dress; only Brahmins wore white layered robes as a mark of their caste.

sentences.zh: 死者或焚屍取灰，以為浮圖；

translations.literal: For the dead, some burn the corpse and take the ashes to make a stupa;
translations.idiomatic: Some disposed of the dead by cremation, placing the ashes in a stupa;

sentences.zh: 或委之中野，以施禽獸；

translations.literal: some cast them in the open wilds to give to birds and beasts;
translations.idiomatic: others left the body in the open country for birds and beasts;

sentences.zh: 或流之於河，以飼魚鱉。

translations.literal: some cast them into rivers to feed fish and turtles.
translations.idiomatic: still others cast the body into rivers to feed fish and turtles.

sentences.zh: 無喪紀之文。

translations.literal: There are no mourning rites in writing.
translations.idiomatic: No written code of mourning rites was kept.

sentences.zh: 謀反者幽殺之，小犯罰錢以贖罪。

translations.literal: Those who plot rebellion are secretly put to death; minor offenses are fined in money to redeem guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels were executed in secret; lesser offenses were punished by fines paid in coin.

sentences.zh: 不孝則斷手刖足，截耳割鼻，放流邊外。

translations.literal: For unfilial conduct the hands are severed and feet cut off, ears cut and noses sliced, and one is banished beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Unfilial conduct was punished by mutilation—severed hands, amputated feet, cropped ears, sliced noses—and exile beyond the borders.

sentences.zh: 有文字，善天文算歷之術。

translations.literal: They have writing and are skilled in the arts of astronomy, calculation, and calendrics.
translations.idiomatic: They had a written language and were adept at astronomy, mathematics, and calendrical science.

sentences.zh: 其人皆學《悉曇章》，云是梵天法。

translations.literal: The people all study the Siddham Chapter, saying it is the law of Brahma Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone studied the Siddham script, which they held to be the sacred law of Brahma.

sentences.zh: 書於貝多樹葉以紀事。

translations.literal: They write on pattra tree leaves to record affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Records were written on pattra-leaf pages.

sentences.zh: 不殺生飲酒。

translations.literal: They do not kill living things or drink wine.
translations.idiomatic: They abstained from killing and from wine.

sentences.zh: 國中往往有舊佛跡。

translations.literal: Throughout the state there are often traces of the Buddha of old.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient traces of the Buddha were found throughout the land.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝時，遣裴矩應接西蕃，諸國多有至者，唯天竺不通，帝以為恨。

translations.literal: In Emperor Yang of Sui's time, Pei Ju was sent to receive the Western Barbarians; many states came, but only India did not communicate—the emperor took this as a regret.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Yang of Sui, Pei Ju was dispatched to receive Western envoys. Many kingdoms sent missions, but India alone remained out of contact—a source of regret to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 當武德中，其國大亂。

translations.literal: During Wude, that state fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude reign the country was torn by civil war.

sentences.zh: 其嗣王屍邏逸多練兵聚眾，所向無敵。

translations.literal: The heir-king Shiluoyiduo drilled troops and gathered masses; wherever he turned there was no enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The heir Shiluoyiduo drilled armies and gathered followers, sweeping all before him without defeat.

sentences.zh: 象不解鞍，人不釋甲，居六載而四天竺之君皆北面以臣之，威勢遠振，刑政甚肅。

translations.literal: Elephants did not remove saddles; men did not lay aside armor. Within six years the rulers of the four Indias all turned north to serve him as subjects; his awesome power shook the distant regions and punishments and government were very strict.
translations.idiomatic: For six years elephants never shed their howdahs and soldiers never laid down their armor. Within that time the rulers of all four Indias submitted and faced north as his vassals. His authority resounded across the subcontinent, and his rule was sternly enforced.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十五年，屍羅逸多自稱摩伽陀王，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhenguan, Shiraditya styled himself King of Magadha and sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Zhenguan, Shiraditya styled himself King of Magadha and dispatched a tribute mission.

sentences.zh: 太宗降璽書慰問，屍羅逸多大驚，問諸國人曰：「自古曾有摩訶震旦使人至吾國乎？」

translations.literal: Taizong sent down an imperial letter of inquiry and consolation; Shiraditya was greatly astonished and asked the people of his state, saying: "Since antiquity has an envoy of Great China ever reached our state?
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent an imperial letter of greeting. Shiraditya was astonished and asked his courtiers: "Has an envoy from Great China ever reached our kingdom before?

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「未之有也。」

translations.literal: All said: "Never has there been such a thing."
translations.idiomatic: They all answered: "Never."

sentences.zh: 乃膜拜而受詔書，因遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bowed in worship and received the edict, and sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He then prostrated himself to receive the edict and sent another tribute mission in return.

sentences.zh: 太宗以其地遠，禮之甚厚，復遣衛尉丞李義表報使。

translations.literal: Taizong, because its land was distant, treated it with great courtesy and again dispatched Weiwei Assistant Director Li Yibiao as a return envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Because India lay so far away, Taizong treated the mission with exceptional honor and sent Li Yibiao of the Court of Imperial Regalia as a return envoy.

sentences.zh: 屍羅逸多遣大臣郊迎，傾城邑以縱觀，焚香夾道，逸多率其臣下東面拜受敕書，復遣使獻火珠及郁金香、菩提樹。

translations.literal: Shiraditya sent great ministers to welcome him at the suburbs; the whole city poured out to watch; incense burned along both sides of the road; Shiraditya led his ministers to face east and bow to receive the edict, and again sent envoys presenting fire pearls, tulips, and a bodhi tree.
translations.idiomatic: Shiraditya sent ministers to greet Li Yibiao beyond the walls, and the whole city turned out to watch. Incense lined the roads. Shiraditya led his court to face east and receive the imperial letter, then sent fresh envoys bearing fire pearls, tulips, and a bodhi tree.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十年，沙門玄奘至其國，將梵本經論六百餘部而歸。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenguan, the monk Xuanzang reached that state and returned bearing more than six hundred volumes of Buddhist sutras and treatises in the Sanskrit original.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Zhenguan the monk Xuanzang reached India and returned with more than six hundred volumes of Sanskrit scriptures and treatises.

sentences.zh: 先是遣右率府長史王玄策使天竺，其四天竺國王咸遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Earlier the Right Commandant of the Left Guard Chief Administrator Wang Xuance had been sent as envoy to India; the kings of the four Indias all sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Xuance, chief administrator of the Right Commandant of the Left Guard, had been sent as envoy to India, and the kings of all four Indias had dispatched tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 會中天竺王屍羅逸多死，國中大亂，其臣那伏帝阿羅那順篡立，乃盡發胡兵以拒玄策。

translations.literal: It happened that the Middle India king Shiraditya died and the state fell into great disorder; his minister Navaditya Arunadasy usurped the throne and thereupon mustered all foreign troops to resist Xuance.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Shiraditya of Middle India died and the country plunged into chaos. His minister Arunadasy seized the throne and mobilized every available force to repel Xuance.

sentences.zh: 玄策從騎三十人與胡禦戰，不敵，矢盡，悉被擒。

translations.literal: Xuance with thirty mounted followers fought the foreigners in defense; they could not prevail; arrows were exhausted; all were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Xuance and his thirty mounted escorts fought the Indian forces but were overwhelmed. When their arrows ran out, all were taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 胡並掠諸國貢獻之物。

translations.literal: The foreigners also plundered the tribute goods of the various states.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels also looted the tribute goods that the other kingdoms had sent.

sentences.zh: 玄策乃挺身宵遁，走至吐蕃，發精銳一千二百人，並泥婆羅國七千餘騎，以從玄策。

translations.literal: Xuance thereupon slipped away alone by night, fled to Tibet, and raised twelve hundred picked troops, together with more than seven thousand horsemen of Nepal, to follow Xuance.
translations.idiomatic: Xuance escaped alone under cover of night and made his way to Tibet, where he raised twelve hundred elite troops and more than seven thousand Nepalese cavalry to follow him.

sentences.zh: 玄策與副使蔣師仁率二國兵進至中天竺國城，連戰三日，大破之，斬首三千餘級，赴水溺死者且萬人，阿羅那順棄城而遁，師仁進擒獲之。

translations.literal: Xuance and Vice-Envoy Jiang Shiren led the troops of the two states and advanced to the capital of Middle India; they fought three days in succession and routed the enemy; more than three thousand heads were cut off; those who drowned fleeing into the water approached ten thousand; Arunadasy abandoned the city and fled; Shiren pressed forward and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuance and his deputy Jiang Shiren led the combined Tibetan and Nepalese forces to the capital of Middle India. After three days of battle they routed the enemy, killing more than three thousand and drowning nearly ten thousand in flight. Arunadasy abandoned the city and fled, but Jiang Shiren pursued and captured him.

sentences.zh: 虜男女萬二千人，牛馬三萬餘頭匹。

translations.literal: Captives numbered twelve thousand men and women; cattle and horses more than thirty thousand head.
translations.idiomatic: They took twelve thousand captives and more than thirty thousand head of cattle and horses.

sentences.zh: 於是天竺震懼，俘阿羅那順以歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon India was shaken with fear; Arunadasy was taken captive and brought back.
translations.idiomatic: India was shaken with fear. Arunadasy was taken prisoner and brought back to Tang.

sentences.zh: 二十二年至京師，太宗大悅，命有司告宗廟，而謂群臣曰：「夫人耳目玩於聲色，口鼻耽於臭味，此乃敗德之源。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year they reached the capital; Taizong was greatly pleased and ordered the officials to announce it to the ancestral temple; and he said to the assembled ministers: "When a man's eyes and ears indulge in sound and color, and mouth and nose are steeped in flavors and odors, this is the source of ruined virtue.
translations.idiomatic: They reached the capital in the twenty-second year. Taizong was delighted and ordered the rites reported to the ancestral temple. Addressing his ministers, he said: "When eyes and ears are lost in pleasure and mouth and nose are steeped in indulgence, virtue is undone at the root.

sentences.zh: 若婆羅門不劫掠我使人，豈為俘虜耶？

translations.literal: If the Brahmins had not plundered our envoy, how would they have become captives?
translations.idiomatic: Had the Brahmins not robbed our envoy, would they now be captives?

sentences.zh: 昔中山以貪寶取弊，蜀侯以金牛致滅，莫不由之。」

translations.literal: Formerly Zhongshan met ruin through greed for treasure; the Lord of Shu brought destruction through the golden ox—all alike came to grief by this path.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan was ruined by greed for treasure; the Lord of Shu was destroyed by the golden ox. Every such fall follows the same road.

sentences.zh: 拜玄策朝散大夫。

translations.literal: Xuance was appointed Gentleman for Promoting Good Governance.
translations.idiomatic: Xuance was appointed Gentleman for Promoting Good Governance.

sentences.zh: 是時就其國得方土那邇娑婆寐，自言壽二百歲，云有長生之術。

translations.literal: At this time from that state there was obtained the alchemist Narendrasena, who declared his age to be two hundred years and claimed to possess the art of long life.
translations.idiomatic: At that time an alchemist named Narendrasena was brought from India. He claimed to be two hundred years old and professed to know the secret of immortality.

sentences.zh: 太宗深加禮敬，館之於金飈門內。

translations.literal: Taizong treated him with deep courtesy and lodged him within the Jinbiao Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong received him with great honor and housed him inside the Jinbiao Gate.

sentences.zh: 造延年之藥。

translations.literal: He prepared a life-prolonging elixir.
translations.idiomatic: There he prepared an elixir of longevity.

sentences.zh: 令兵部尚書崔敦禮監主之，發使天下，采諸奇藥異石，不可稱數。

translations.literal: The Minister of War Cui Dunli was ordered to supervise it; envoys were sent throughout the realm to gather every sort of marvelous drug and exotic stone—beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Cui Dunli was appointed to supervise the work, and envoys were dispatched across the empire to gather rare drugs and exotic stones beyond number.

sentences.zh: 延歷歲月，藥成，服竟不效，後放還本國。

translations.literal: Months and years passed; when the elixir was finished and taken, it proved wholly ineffective; afterward he was sent back to his native state.
translations.idiomatic: Months passed before the elixir was ready, but when it was taken it had no effect. Narendrasena was eventually sent home.

sentences.zh: 太宗之葬昭陵也，刻石像阿羅那順之形，列於玄闕之下。

translations.literal: When Taizong was buried at Zhaoling, a stone image of Arunadasy's form was carved and arrayed below the Spirit Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong was buried at Zhaoling, a stone likeness of Arunadasy was carved and placed before the Spirit Gate.

sentences.zh: 五天竺所屬之國數十，風俗物產略同。

translations.literal: The states subject to the five Indias number several tens; customs and products are broadly alike.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen kingdoms were subject to the five Indias, and their customs and products were broadly similar.

sentences.zh: 有伽沒路國，其俗開東門以向日。

translations.literal: There is the state of Kamarupa; its custom is to open the east gate toward the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Among them was Kamarupa, whose people opened the eastern gate to face the rising sun.

sentences.zh: 王玄策至，其王發使貢以奇珍異物及地圖，因請老子像及《道德經》。

translations.literal: When Wang Xuance arrived, its king sent envoys presenting rare treasures and exotic objects and a map, and requested a statue of Laozi and the Daodejing.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Xuance arrived, the king sent envoys bearing rare treasures and a map, and asked for a statue of Laozi and a copy of the Daodejing.

sentences.zh: 那揭陀國，有醯羅城，中有重閣，藏佛頂骨及錫杖。

translations.literal: In the state of Nalanda there is Hirapura; within it is a multi-storied pavilion storing the Buddha's cranial bone and his iron staff.
translations.idiomatic: In Nalanda stood the city of Hirapura, where a multi-storied pavilion housed the Buddha's cranial relic and his iron staff.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二十年，遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Zhenguan, envoys were sent presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Zhenguan it sent envoys bearing local products as tribute.

sentences.zh: 天授二年，東天竺王摩羅枝摩、西天竺王屍羅逸多、南天竺王遮婁其拔羅婆、北天竺王婁其那那、中天竺王地婆西那，並來朝獻。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianshou, the East India king Molozhimo, the West India king Shiraditya, the South India king Zhelouqibaluopo, the North India king Louqinanana, and the Middle India king Diboxina all came to court with offerings.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianshou the kings of East, West, South, North, and Middle India—Molozhimo, Shiraditya, Zhelouqibaluopo, Louqinanana, and Diboxina—all came to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 景龍四年，南天竺國復遣使來朝。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jinglong, South India again sent envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jinglong South India again sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，復遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyun, envoys were again sent presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingyun it again sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 開元二年，西天竺復遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan, West India again sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyuan West India again sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 八年，南天竺國遣使獻五色能言鸚鵡。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, South India sent envoys presenting a five-colored talking parrot.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year South India sent a five-colored parrot that could speak.

sentences.zh: 其年，南天竺國王屍利那羅僧伽請以戰象及兵馬討大食及吐蕃等，仍求有及名其軍。

translations.literal: That year, the South India king Shilinaluosengqie requested to use war elephants and troops and horses to attack the Arabs, Tibet, and others, and also asked that officials name his army.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the South Indian king Shilinaluosengqie offered war elephants and troops to campaign against the Arabs, Tibet, and others, and asked that the court confer a name upon his army.

sentences.zh: 玄宗甚嘉之，名軍為懷德軍。

translations.literal: Xuanzong greatly approved and named the army the Army of Cherished Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong was much pleased and named the force the Army of Cherished Virtue.

sentences.zh: 九月，南天竺王屍利那羅僧伽寶多枝摩為國造寺，上表乞寺額，敕以歸化為名賜之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the South India king Shilinaluosengqie Baoduozhimo built a temple for the state, submitted a memorial requesting a temple plaque, and an edict bestowed the name Guihua upon it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the South Indian king Shilinaluosengqie Baoduozhimo built a temple for his kingdom and petitioned for an official name. The emperor granted the name Return to Civilization.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遣使冊利那羅伽寶多為南天竺國王，遣使來朝。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, envoys were sent to invest Linaluojiabaoduo as King of South India; envoys came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month envoys were sent to invest Linaluojiabaoduo as king of South India, and a mission came to pay court.

sentences.zh: 十七年六月，北天竺國藏沙門僧密多獻質汗等藥。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventeenth year, the North India Tripitaka monk Miduo presented drugs such as zhihan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the seventeenth year the Tripitaka monk Miduo of North India presented medicines including zhihan.

sentences.zh: 十九年十月，中天竺國王伊沙伏摩遣其大德僧來朝貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the nineteenth year, the Middle India king Yishafumo sent his great virtue monk to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the nineteenth year the Middle Indian king Yishafumo sent a senior monk to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 二十九年三月，中天竺王子李承恩來朝，授遊擊將軍，放還。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-ninth year, the Middle India prince Li Chengen came to court, was appointed General of Mobile Striking Force, and was sent back.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twenty-ninth year the Middle Indian prince Li Chengen came to court, was appointed General of Mobile Striking Force, and was sent home.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，累遣使來。

translations.literal: During Tianbao, envoys were repeatedly sent.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao reign tribute missions came repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 罽賓國

translations.literal: The Kingdom of Kapisa
translations.idiomatic: Kapisa

sentences.zh: 罽賓國，在蔥嶺南，去京師萬二千二百里。

translations.literal: The Kingdom of Kapisa lies south of the Pamirs, twelve thousand two hundred li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Kapisa lay south of the Pamirs, twelve thousand two hundred li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 常役屬於大月氏。

translations.literal: It is regularly subject to and serves the Great Yuezhi.
translations.idiomatic: It was usually subject to the Great Yuezhi.

sentences.zh: 其地暑濕，人皆乘象，土宜秔稻，草木淩寒不死。

translations.literal: Its land is hot and damp; the people all ride elephants; the soil suits long-grain rice; grasses and trees withstand cold without dying.
translations.idiomatic: The land was hot and humid. People traveled by elephant, long-grain rice flourished in the soil, and vegetation survived even severe cold.

sentences.zh: 其俗尤信佛法。

translations.literal: Its customs especially believe in the Buddhist Law.
translations.idiomatic: The people were especially devoted to Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝時，引致西域，前後至者三十余國，唯罽賓不至。

translations.literal: In Emperor Yang of Sui's time, the Western Regions were summoned; more than thirty states came before and after, but only Kapisa did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Yang of Sui more than thirty Western kingdoms sent missions, but Kapisa alone stayed away.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十一年，遣使獻名馬，太宗嘉其誠款，賜以繒彩。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhenguan, envoys were sent presenting famed horses; Taizong praised their sincere good faith and bestowed colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Zhenguan it sent famed horses as tribute. Taizong commended its sincerity and rewarded it with silk.

sentences.zh: 十六年，又遣使獻褥特鼠，喙尖而尾赤，能食蛇，有被蛇螫者，鼠輒嗅而尿之，其瘡立愈。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, envoys were again sent presenting the rute rat, with pointed beak and red tail, able to eat snakes; when someone was bitten by a snake, the rat would sniff and urinate on the wound, and the sore was immediately healed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year it sent the rute rat—a creature with a pointed snout and red tail that ate snakes. When someone was snake-bitten, the rat would sniff the wound and urinate on it, and the injury healed at once.

sentences.zh: 顯慶三年，訪其國俗，雲「王始祖馨孽，至今曷擷支，父子傳位，已十二代。」

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianqing, its state customs were inquired into; it was said: "The founding king was Xinnie; down to the present Hejiezhi, father and son have transmitted the throne through twelve generations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianqing an inquiry into local custom reported: "The founding king was Xinnie; the present ruler is Hejiezhi. The throne has passed from father to son through twelve generations.

sentences.zh: 其年，改其城為修鮮都督府。

translations.literal: That year, its city was changed into the Xiuxian Protectorate Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That year its capital was made the Xiuxian Protectorate Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 龍朔初，授其王修鮮等十一州諸軍事兼修鮮都督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longshuo, its king was appointed Commander over all military affairs of the eleven prefectures including Xiuxian, and concurrently Protector of Xiuxian.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longshuo reign its king was appointed commander of military affairs for the eleven prefectures including Xiuxian and concurrently Protector of Xiuxian.

sentences.zh: 勃律國

translations.literal: The Kingdom of Bolü
translations.idiomatic: Bolü

sentences.zh: 又有勃律國，在罽賓、吐蕃之間。

translations.literal: There is also the state of Bolü, lying between Kapisa and Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Bolü, situated between Kapisa and Tibet.

sentences.zh: 開元中頻遣使朝獻。

translations.literal: During Kaiyuan envoys were frequently sent to court with offerings.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign it sent tribute missions frequently.

sentences.zh: 八年，冊立其王蘇麟陀逸之為勃律國王，朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, its king Sulintuoyizhi was invested as King of Bolü; tribute missions were unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year its king Sulintuoyizhi was invested as king of Bolü, and tribute continued without interruption.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，為吐蕃所破。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, it was broken by Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year it was destroyed by Tibet.

sentences.zh: 康國，即漢康居之國也。

translations.literal: Kang is the state of Han's Kangju.
translations.idiomatic: Kang was the kingdom known in Han times as Kangju.

sentences.zh: 其王姓溫，月氏人也。

translations.literal: Its king bears the surname Wen; he is a man of the Yuezhi.
translations.idiomatic: The royal house bore the surname Wen and was of Yuezhi descent.

sentences.zh: 先居張掖祁連山北昭武城，為突厥所破，南依蔥嶺，遂有其地。

translations.literal: Formerly they dwelt at Zhaowu City north of the Qilian Mountains in Zhangye; broken by the Turks, they relied on the Pamirs to the south and thereby came to hold this land.
