translations.idiomatic: They had once lived at Zhaowu City north of the Qilian Mountains in Zhangye. Driven south by the Turks, they settled along the Pamirs and took possession of this territory.

sentences.zh: 枝庶皆以昭武為姓氏，不忘本也。

translations.literal: The collateral branches all take Zhaowu as surname, not forgetting their origin.
translations.idiomatic: Cadet branches all took Zhaowu as their surname, preserving memory of their origins.

sentences.zh: 其人皆深目高鼻，多須髯。

translations.literal: The people all have deep-set eyes and high noses, with abundant beards.
translations.idiomatic: The people had deep-set eyes, high noses, and heavy beards.

sentences.zh: 丈夫翦髮或辮髮。

translations.literal: Husbands cut their hair short or wear it in braids.
translations.idiomatic: Men wore their hair cropped short or braided.

sentences.zh: 其王冠氈帽。

translations.literal: Its king wears a felt cap as crown.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore a felt cap.

sentences.zh: 飾以金寶。

translations.literal: It is adorned with gold and jewels.
translations.idiomatic: It was adorned with gold and jewels.

sentences.zh: 婦人盤髻，幪以皁巾，飾以金花。

translations.literal: Women wear coiled topknots, veiled with black kerchiefs and adorned with golden flowers.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore coiled topknots veiled in black kerchiefs and ornamented with gold flowers.

sentences.zh: 人多嗜酒，好歌舞於道路。

translations.literal: The people mostly love wine and delight in song and dance in the roads.
translations.idiomatic: The people were fond of wine and given to singing and dancing in the streets.

sentences.zh: 生子必以石蜜內口中，明膠置掌內，欲其成長口常甘言，掌持錢如膠之黏物。

translations.literal: When a child is born, rock honey must be placed in the mouth and clear glue in the palm, wishing that as it grows the mouth will always speak sweet words and the palm hold money as glue sticks to things.
translations.idiomatic: At birth a child was given rock honey in the mouth and clear glue in the palm—a blessing that it would grow up speaking kindly and grasping wealth as glue clings to what it touches.

sentences.zh: 俗習胡書。

translations.literal: The custom is to practice foreign script.
translations.idiomatic: They used a foreign script.

sentences.zh: 善商賈，爭分銖之利。

translations.literal: They are skilled at trade and contend over profits to the fraction of a coin.
translations.idiomatic: They were skilled merchants who haggled over the smallest profit.

sentences.zh: 男子年二十，即遠之旁國，來適中夏，利之所在，無所不到。

translations.literal: When a man reaches twenty years, he goes far to neighboring states and comes to the Middle Kingdom; wherever profit lies, there is nowhere he does not reach.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty a man would travel to neighboring kingdoms and onward to China itself. Wherever profit beckoned, Kang merchants would go.

sentences.zh: 以十二月為歲首，有婆羅門為之占星候氣，以定吉兇。

translations.literal: The twelfth month is taken as the year's beginning; Brahmins observe the stars and watch the qi for them to determine fortune and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: The year began in the twelfth month. Brahmins read the stars and watched the seasonal qi to determine good and ill fortune.

sentences.zh: 頗有佛法。

translations.literal: There is considerably the Buddhist Law.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism was also widely practiced.

sentences.zh: 至十一月，鼓舞乞寒，以水相潑，盛為戲樂。

translations.literal: By the eleventh month they beat drums and dance begging off the cold, splashing water on one another—a great amusement.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month they held the Cold-Dispelling Festival with drumming, dancing, and water-splashing—a great communal revel.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝時，其王屈術支娶西突厥葉護可汗女，遂臣於西突厥。

translations.literal: In Emperor Yang of Sui's time, its king Qushuzhi married a daughter of the Western Turk Yabghu Qaghan and thereupon became subject to the Western Turks.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Yang of Sui, King Qushuzhi married a daughter of the Western Turk Yabghu Qaghan and thereafter submitted to the Western Turks.

sentences.zh: 武德十年，屈術支遣使獻名馬。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Wude, Qushuzhi sent envoys presenting famed horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Wude Qushuzhi sent famed horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 貞觀九年，又遣使貢獅子，太宗嘉其遠至，命秘書監虞世南為之賦，自此朝貢歲至。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenguan, they again sent envoys presenting lions. Emperor Taizong praised their coming from afar and ordered Secretary Director Yu Shinan to compose a rhapsody for the occasion. From then on tribute missions came every year.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 9 Kang sent lions as tribute. Taizong, delighted at their journey from so far away, had Yu Shinan compose a rhapsody in their honor; thereafter tribute arrived annually.

sentences.zh: 十一年，又獻金桃、銀桃，詔令植之於苑囿。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, they again presented golden peaches and silver peaches; an edict ordered them planted in the imperial parks.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year they presented golden and silver peaches, and the court ordered them planted in the palace gardens.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天年，則天封其大首領篤婆缽提為康國王，仍拜左驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Wansui Tongtian era, Empress Zetian enfeoffed their great chieftain Dubo Boti as King of Kang and also appointed him General-in-Chief of the Left Xiaowei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wansui Tongtian era Wu Zetian enfeoffed the great chieftain Dubo Boti as King of Kang and made him General-in-Chief of the Left Xiaowei Guard.

sentences.zh: 缽提尋卒，又冊其子泥涅師師為康國王。

translations.literal: Boti soon died, and his son Nienishi was again enfeoffed as King of Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Boti died soon after, and the court enfeoffed his son Nienishi as King of Kang.

sentences.zh: 師師以神龍中卒，國人又立突昏為王。

translations.literal: Shishi died in the Shenlong era, and the people of the state again established Tuhun as king.
translations.idiomatic: Nienishi died during the Shenlong reign, and the Kang people enthroned Tuhun as king.

sentences.zh: 開元六年，遣使貢獻鎖子甲、水精杯、馬腦瓶、駝鳥卵及越諾之類。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaiyuan, envoys were sent presenting chain-mail armor, crystal cups, agate bottles, ostrich eggs, and the like of Yuenuo.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 6 envoys brought chain-mail armor, crystal cups, agate bottles, ostrich eggs, and other exotic goods including Yuenuo cloth.

sentences.zh: 十九年，其王烏勒上表，請封其子咄曷為曹國王，默啜為米國王，許之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, its king Wule submitted a memorial requesting that his son Duoge be enfeoffed as King of Cao and Mochuo as King of Mi; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 19 King Wule petitioned to have his son Duoge enfeoffed as King of Cao and Mochuo as King of Mi; the court granted both requests.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，烏勒卒，遣使冊咄曷襲父位。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, Wule died; envoys were sent to invest Duoge to succeed his father's position.
translations.idiomatic: Wule died in Kaiyuan 27, and envoys were dispatched to invest Duoge as his successor.

sentences.zh: 天寶三年，又封為欽化王，其母可敦封為郡夫人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianbao, he was again enfeoffed as Prince of Qinhua, and his mother the Khatun was enfeoffed as Lady of a Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 3 he was further enfeoffed as Prince of Qinhua, and his mother the Khatun was made Lady of a Commandery.

sentences.zh: 十一載、十三載，並遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the eleventh and thirteenth years, tribute missions were both sent to court.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute missions were sent in Tianbao 11 and Tianbao 13.

sentences.zh: 波斯國

translations.literal: The State of Persia
translations.idiomatic: Persia

sentences.zh: 波斯國，在京師西一萬五千三百里，東與吐火羅、康國接，北鄰突厥之可薩部，西北拒拂菻，正西及南俱臨大海。

translations.literal: The state of Persia lies fifteen thousand three hundred li west of the capital. To the east it borders Tuhuoluo and Kang; to the north it neighbors the Khazars of the Turks; to the northwest it faces Fulin; due west and south it all adjoins the great sea.
translations.idiomatic: Persia lay fifteen thousand three hundred li west of the capital, bordering Tuhuoluo and Kang to the east, the Turkic Khazars to the north, and Fulin to the northwest; its western and southern frontiers all faced the open sea.

sentences.zh: 戶數十萬。

translations.literal: Households number in the hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom had hundreds of thousands of households.

sentences.zh: 其王居有二城，復有大城十余，猶中國之離宮。

translations.literal: Its king dwells in two cities, and furthermore has more than ten great cities, like detached palaces in China.
translations.idiomatic: The king maintained two capitals and more than ten major cities, rather like the detached palaces of China.

sentences.zh: 其王初嗣位，便密選子才堪承統者，書其名字，封而藏之。

translations.literal: When its king first succeeds to the throne, he secretly selects a son whose talent can bear the succession, writes his name, seals it, and hides it.
translations.idiomatic: Upon acceding, the king secretly chose whichever son seemed fit to inherit, wrote down the name, sealed it, and kept it hidden.

sentences.zh: 王死後，大臣與王之群子共發封而視之，奉所書名者為主焉。

translations.literal: After the king dies, grand ministers together with the king's sons jointly open the seal and look; they enthroned whomever's name was written.
translations.idiomatic: After the king's death, ministers and royal sons opened the sealed name together and enthroned the prince it named.

sentences.zh: 其王冠金花冠，坐獅子床，服錦袍，加以瓔珞。

translations.literal: Its king wears a golden-flower crown, sits on a lion couch, wears brocade robes, and is further adorned with necklaces.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore a crown of golden flowers, sat upon a lion throne, dressed in brocade robes, and was hung with jeweled necklaces.

sentences.zh: 俗事天地日月水火之諸神，西域諸胡事火祅者，皆詣波斯受法焉。

translations.literal: The custom is to serve the gods of Heaven and Earth, sun and moon, water and fire; all the Western Region Hu who serve Fire Zoroastrianism go to Persia to receive the Law.
translations.idiomatic: They worshiped the gods of heaven and earth, sun and moon, water and fire; Western peoples who practiced Zoroastrian fire worship all went to Persia to receive the faith.

sentences.zh: 其事神，以麝香和蘇塗須點額，及於耳鼻，用以為敬，拜必交股。

translations.literal: In serving the gods, musk mixed with ghee is smeared to dot the forehead and also on the nose and ears, using this as reverence; when bowing one must cross the thighs.
translations.idiomatic: In worship they anointed forehead, nose, and ears with musk mixed in ghee as a mark of reverence and bowed with legs crossed.

sentences.zh: 文字同於諸胡。

translations.literal: The script is the same as that of the various Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Their writing was the same as that of other Western peoples.

sentences.zh: 男女皆徒跣。

translations.literal: Men and women all go barefoot.
translations.idiomatic: Both men and women went barefoot.

sentences.zh: 丈夫翦髮，戴白皮帽，衣不開襟，並有巾帔，多用蘇方青白色為之，兩邊緣以織成錦。

translations.literal: Husbands cut their hair short, wear white felt caps, and dress in garments that do not open at the front; they also have kerchiefs and shawls, mostly made in indigo and white from sappanwood, with woven brocade edging both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Men wore their hair cropped, white felt caps, and closed-front robes with kerchiefs and shawls—usually dyed indigo or white with sappanwood and edged in woven brocade.

sentences.zh: 婦人亦巾帔裙衫，辮髮垂後，飾以金銀，其國乘象而戰，每一象，戰士百人，有敗恤者則盡殺之。

translations.literal: Women also wear kerchiefs, shawls, skirts, and jackets, with braided hair hanging behind and adorned in gold and silver. The state fights mounted on elephants; for each elephant there are a hundred warriors, and if any are defeated and ashamed they are all put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Women dressed in kerchiefs, shawls, skirts, and jackets, their braided hair hanging down and ornamented with gold and silver. In war the Persians fought from elephants, each supported by a hundred warriors; any who suffered defeat were executed without exception.

sentences.zh: 國人生女，年十歲已上有姿貌者，其王收而養之，以賞有功之臣。

translations.literal: When the state produces daughters, those ten years of age or older who have beauty the king takes and rears, to reward meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The king collected girls of ten or older who showed beauty, reared them at court, and bestowed them upon ministers who had earned merit.

sentences.zh: 俗右尊而左卑。

translations.literal: The custom holds the right honorable and the left lowly.
translations.idiomatic: By custom the right was honored and the left subordinate.

sentences.zh: 以六月一日為歲首。

translations.literal: The first day of the sixth month is taken as the year's beginning.
translations.idiomatic: The new year began on the first day of the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 斷獄不為文書約束，口決於庭。

translations.literal: Judging cases is not bound by written documents; judgment is spoken in court.
translations.idiomatic: Cases were decided orally in court without reliance on written pleadings.

sentences.zh: 其系囚無年限，唯王者代立則釋之。

translations.literal: Their imprisoned have no term limit; only when a king is replaced by succession are they released.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners were held indefinitely and released only when a new king succeeded.

sentences.zh: 其叛逆之罪，就火祅燒鐵灼其舌，瘡白者為理直，瘡黑者為有罪。

translations.literal: For the crime of rebellion, before the fire altar iron is heated and the tongue burned; if the sore is white the person is deemed in the right, if black guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels were tried at the fire altar by burning iron pressed to the tongue: a white blister meant innocence, a black one guilt.

sentences.zh: 其刑有斷手、刖足、髡鉗、劓刖，輕罪翦須，或系牌於項以誌之，經時月而釋焉。

translations.literal: Their punishments include cutting off the hand, amputating the foot, shaving the head and fettering, cutting off the nose and amputating the foot; for light offenses the beard is cut, or a placard is tied at the neck as a mark, and after months they are released.
translations.idiomatic: Penalties ranged from amputation of hands and feet to nose-cutting, head-shaving with fetters, and beard-clipping for lesser crimes; some offenders wore placards at the neck for months before release.

sentences.zh: 其強盜一入獄，至老更不出，小盜罰以銀錢。

translations.literal: Once a robber enters prison he never comes out until old age; petty theft is punished with silver money.
translations.idiomatic: Major robbers were imprisoned for life; petty thieves paid fines in silver.

sentences.zh: 死亡則棄之於山，制服一月而即吉。

translations.literal: When someone dies the body is cast upon the mountains; mourning dress is worn for one month and then auspicious rites resume.
translations.idiomatic: The dead were left on the mountains; mourners wore funeral garb for a month before returning to ordinary life.

sentences.zh: 氣候暑熱，土地寬平，知耕種，多畜牧，有鳥形如橐駝，飛不能高，食草及肉，亦能噉犬攫羊，土人極以為患。

translations.literal: The climate is hot, the land broad and level; they know cultivation and keep much livestock. There is a bird shaped like a camel that cannot fly high, eating grass and meat; it can also devour dogs and seize sheep, and the natives greatly regard it as a pest.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was sweltering and the land broad and fertile; agriculture and herding both flourished. A camel-shaped bird that flew low fed on grass and flesh and even preyed on dogs and sheep, to the natives' great distress.

sentences.zh: 又多白馬、駿犬，或赤日行七百里者駮，金犬今所謂波斯犬也。

translations.literal: There are also many white horses and fine hounds, or piebald horses that can run seven hundred li in a day when red; golden hounds are what are now called Persian hounds.
translations.idiomatic: White horses and swift hounds abounded, along with piebald steeds said to cover seven hundred li in a day; the golden hounds are what we now call Persian dogs.

sentences.zh: 出䮫及大驢、師子、白象、珊瑚樹高一二尺，琥珀、車渠、瑪瑙、火珠、玻璃、琉璃、無食子、香附子、訶黎勒、胡椒、蓽撥、石蜜、千年棗、甘露桃。

translations.literal: They produce camels and great donkeys, lions, white elephants, coral trees one or two chi high, amber, giant clams, agate, fire pearls, glass, lapis lazuli, myrobalan, cyperus, chebulic myrobalan, pepper, long pepper, rock honey, millennial jujubes, and honey peaches.
translations.idiomatic: Exports included camels and great donkeys, lions, white elephants, coral trees a foot or two tall, amber, giant clams, agate, fire pearls, glass, lapis lazuli, myrobalan, cyperus, chebulic myrobalan, pepper, long pepper, rock honey, millennial jujubes, and honey peaches.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，西突厥葉護可汗頻擊破其國，波斯王庫薩和為西突厥所殺，其子施利立，葉護因分其部帥，監統其國，波斯竟臣於葉護。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye of Sui, the Western Turk Yabghu Qaghan repeatedly broke their state. The Persian king Kusahe was killed by the Western Turks; his son Shili was established. Yabghu therefore divided their tribal chiefs to supervise and govern the state, and Persia ultimately became subject to Yabghu.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of Emperor Yang's Daye reign the Western Turk Yabghu Qaghan repeatedly crushed Persia. King Kusahe was killed; his son Shili was enthroned, but Yabghu partitioned the realm among his own chieftains to rule it, and Persia fell under Turkic domination.

sentences.zh: 及葉護可汗死，其所令監統者因自擅於波斯，不復役屬於西突厥。

translations.literal: When Yabghu Qaghan died, those he had appointed to supervise Persia thereupon seized power there on their own and no longer served the Western Turks.
translations.idiomatic: After Yabghu's death the Turkic governors he had left in Persia seized power for themselves and ceased obeying the Western Turks.

sentences.zh: 施利立一年卒，乃立庫薩和之女為王，突厥又殺之。

translations.literal: Shili reigned one year and died; then Kusahe's daughter was established as queen, and the Turks killed her again.
translations.idiomatic: Shili died after a year on the throne; Kusahe's daughter was then made queen, but the Turks killed her as well.

sentences.zh: 施利之子單羯方奔拂菻，於是國人迎而立之，是為尹恆支，在位二年而卒。

translations.literal: Shili's son Danjiefang fled to Fulin; thereupon the people of the state welcomed and established him—this was Yin Hengzhi, who reigned two years and died.
translations.idiomatic: Shili's son Danjiefang fled to Fulin; the Persians recalled him and enthroned him as Yin Hengzhi, who reigned two years and died.

sentences.zh: 兄子伊嗣候立。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Yisi Hou was established.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Yisi Hou succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳三年，令吏部侍郎裴行儉將兵冊送卑路斯為波斯王，行儉以其路遠，至安西碎葉而還，卑路斯獨返，不得入其國，漸為大食所侵，客於吐火羅國二十余年，有部落數千人，後漸離散。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yifeng, Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Appointments Pei Xingjian was ordered to lead troops to invest and escort Peroz as King of Persia. Xingjian, because the route was far, reached Suyab in Anxi and returned; Peroz returned alone, unable to enter his state, was gradually invaded by Dashi, and sojourned in Tuhuoluo for more than twenty years with a tribe of several thousand men, later gradually scattering.
translations.idiomatic: In Yifeng 3 Pei Xingjian was sent with an army to invest Peroz as King of Persia. Finding the route too long, he turned back at Suyab in the Western Regions; Peroz returned alone but could not re-enter his kingdom. Gradually overrun by the Arabs, he lived as a guest in Tuhuoluo for more than twenty years with a following of several thousand, which later dispersed.

sentences.zh: 至景龍二年，又來入朝，拜為左威衛將軍，無何病卒，其國遂滅，而部眾猶存。

translations.literal: By the second year of Jinglong he again came to court and was appointed General of the Left Weiwu Guard; before long he died of illness. His state was thereby extinguished, though tribal groups still survived.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinglong 2 Peroz came to court again and was made General of the Left Weiwu Guard; he soon died of illness. The Persian kingdom was extinguished, though scattered clans remained.

sentences.zh: 自開元十年至天寶六載，凡十遣使來朝，並獻方物。

translations.literal: From the tenth year of Kaiyuan to the sixth year of Tianbao, in all ten missions came to court, all presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: From Kaiyuan 10 through Tianbao 6, ten embassies arrived at court bearing regional goods.

sentences.zh: 四月，遣使獻瑪瑙床。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, envoys were sent presenting an agate couch.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month an embassy presented an agate couch.

sentences.zh: 九年四月，獻火毛繡舞筵、長毛繡舞筵、無孔真珠。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the ninth year, they presented fire-fur embroidered dance mats, long-fur embroidered dance mats, and flawless pearls.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the ninth year they sent fire-fur and long-fur embroidered dance mats and flawless pearls.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年，波斯與大食同寇廣州，劫倉庫，焚廬舍，浮海而去。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan, Persia together with Dashi raided Guangzhou, plundered the storehouses, burned the buildings, and departed by sea.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan 1 Persian and Arab forces jointly raided Guangzhou, looted the warehouses, burned the buildings, and escaped by sea.

sentences.zh: 大歷六年，遣使來朝，獻真珠等。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dali, envoys came to court presenting pearls and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 6 an embassy came to court with pearls and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 拂菻國

translations.literal: The State of Fulin
translations.idiomatic: Fulin

sentences.zh: 拂菻國，一名大秦，在西海之上，東南與波斯接，地方萬餘里，列城四百，邑居連屬。

translations.literal: The state of Fulin, also called Daqin, lies upon the Western Sea. Southeast it borders Persia; its territory extends more than ten thousand li, with four hundred walled cities and settlements linked in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Fulin, also known as Daqin, stood on the Western Sea. Bordering Persia to the southeast, its domain stretched more than ten thousand li, with four hundred walled cities and linked settlements.

sentences.zh: 其宮宇柱櫳，多以水精琉璃為之。

translations.literal: Its palaces and halls, pillars and balustrades, are mostly made of crystal and glass.
translations.idiomatic: Palace pillars and balustrades were largely fashioned from crystal and glass.

sentences.zh: 有貴臣十二人共治國政，常使一人將囊隨王車，百姓有事者，即以書投囊中，王還宮省發，理其枉直。

translations.literal: Twelve noble ministers jointly govern state affairs; one is always made to carry a bag following the king's carriage. When common people have business, they put writings into the bag; when the king returns to the palace he opens and examines them, judging right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve senior ministers shared governance; one always carried a pouch in the royal train. Citizens dropped petitions into it, and the king reviewed them upon returning to the palace to judge grievances.

sentences.zh: 其王無常人，簡賢者而立之。

translations.literal: Its king is not a fixed person; the worthy are selected and established.
translations.idiomatic: The throne was not hereditary—the worthiest man was chosen to rule.

sentences.zh: 國中災異及風雨不時，輒廢而更立。

translations.literal: When calamities and portents occur in the state, or wind and rain are untimely, the ruler is deposed and another established.
translations.idiomatic: Disasters, omens, or untimely weather led to the ruler's deposition and replacement.

sentences.zh: 其王冠形如鳥舉翼，冠及瓔珞，皆綴以珠寶，著錦繡衣，前不開襟，坐金花床。

translations.literal: Its king's crown is shaped like a bird raising its wings; crown and necklaces are all strung with jewels. He wears brocade robes, the front not opening, and sits on a golden-flower couch.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore a crown shaped like wings outspread, hung with jewels from crown to necklace, brocade robes closed at the front, and sat upon a golden-flower throne.

sentences.zh: 有一鳥似鵝，其毛綠色，常在王邊倚枕上坐，每進食有毒，其鳥輒鳴。

translations.literal: There is a bird like a goose, its feathers green, always sitting beside the king leaning on the pillow. Whenever poison is placed in food, the bird cries out.
translations.idiomatic: A goose-like bird with green feathers perched beside the king's pillow; whenever food was poisoned, the bird cried out.

sentences.zh: 其都城疊石為之，尤絕高峻，凡有十萬余戶，南臨大海。

translations.literal: Its capital is built of piled stone, exceedingly lofty and steep, with more than one hundred thousand households; south it faces the great sea.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was built of stacked stone, towering and steep, with more than one hundred thousand households and the sea to the south.

sentences.zh: 城東面有大門，其高二十余丈，自上及下，飾以黃金，光輝燦爛，連曜數里。

translations.literal: On the east side of the city is a great gate more than twenty zhang high; from top to bottom it is adorned with gold, shining brilliantly and linking its radiance for several li.
translations.idiomatic: On the city's east stood a gate more than twenty zhang high, gilded from summit to base so that its brilliance shone for miles.

sentences.zh: 自外至王室，凡有大門三重，列異寶雕飾。

translations.literal: From the outer precinct to the royal residence there are in all three great gates, arrayed with rare treasures and carved ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Three great gates, each lavishly carved and set with exotic treasures, led from the outer precinct to the royal residence.

sentences.zh: 第二門之樓中，懸一大金秤，以金丸十二枚屬於衡端，以候日之十二時焉；

translations.literal: In the tower of the second gate hangs a great golden scale, with twelve golden balls attached to the beam end to mark the twelve hours of the day;
translations.idiomatic: In the tower of the second gate hung a great golden scale with twelve golden balls at the beam's end to mark the twelve hours of the day;

sentences.zh: 為一金人，其大如人，立於側，每至一時，其金丸輒落，鏗然發聲，引唱以紀日時，毫厘無失。

translations.literal: a golden man, as large as a person, stands at the side; whenever an hour arrives a golden ball falls with a ringing sound, and a voice calls out to record the time, without the slightest error.
translations.idiomatic: beside it stood a life-sized golden figure; at each hour a ball dropped with a clang while a voice announced the time, never missing by the slightest measure.

sentences.zh: 其殿以瑟瑟為柱，黃金為地，象牙為門扇，香木為棟梁。

translations.literal: Its hall uses lapis lazuli for pillars, gold for flooring, ivory for door panels, and fragrant wood for beams and rafters.
translations.idiomatic: The hall had lapis-lazuli pillars, golden floors, ivory doors, and fragrant-wood beams.

sentences.zh: 其俗無瓦，搗白石為末，羅之塗屋上，其堅密光潤，還如玉石。

translations.literal: Their custom has no tile; white stone is pounded to powder, sifted and spread on roofs, becoming as hard, dense, and lustrous as jade stone.
translations.idiomatic: They used no roof tiles; crushed white stone, sifted and plastered over roofs, hardened to a polish like jade.

sentences.zh: 至於盛暑之節，人厭囂熱，乃引水潛流，上遍於屋宇，機制巧密，人莫之知。

translations.literal: In the season of great heat, when people loathe the swelter, water is led in hidden channels flowing upward throughout the buildings; the mechanism is ingeniously precise and no one knows how it works.
translations.idiomatic: In midsummer, when the heat grew unbearable, water was piped in hidden channels through the buildings by mechanisms so ingenious that none could explain them.

sentences.zh: 觀者惟聞屋上泉鳴，俄見四檐飛溜，懸波如瀑，激氣成涼風，其巧妙如此。

translations.literal: Observers only hear springs murmuring on the roofs; suddenly they see flying streams from the four eaves, suspended waves like waterfalls, stirring the air into cool breezes—so clever is the artifice.
translations.idiomatic: One heard only springs murmuring overhead, then saw cascades pour from every eave like waterfalls, stirring cool breezes—such was the ingenuity of the design.

sentences.zh: 風俗，男子翦髮，披帔而右袒，婦人不開襟，錦為頭巾。

translations.literal: Customs: men cut their hair short, wear shawls and bare the right shoulder; women do not open the front of their garments and use brocade as head kerchiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Men cropped their hair, draped shawls, and bared the right shoulder; women wore closed-front dress and brocade head kerchiefs.

sentences.zh: 家資滿億，封以上位。

translations.literal: When household wealth reaches a full hundred million, one is enfeoffed to a superior rank.
translations.idiomatic: Households whose wealth reached a hundred million were ennobled.

sentences.zh: 有羊羔生於土中，其國人候其欲萌，乃築墻以院之，防外獸所食也。

translations.literal: There are lambs born in the earth; the people of the state wait until they are about to sprout, then build walls to enclose them, guarding against being eaten by outside beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Lambs were said to grow from the earth; when they were about to emerge, the people walled the spot to keep wild beasts from devouring them.

sentences.zh: 然其臍與地連，割之則死，唯人著甲走馬及擊鼓以駭之，其羔警鳴而臍絕，便遂水草。

translations.literal: Yet their navels are connected to the ground; if cut they die. Only when men don armor, ride horses, and beat drums to frighten them do the lambs cry out in alarm and the navel sever; then they go to grass and water.
translations.idiomatic: Their navels remained attached to the soil and severing them meant death; only when armored horsemen galloped up beating drums would the lambs cry out, the cord break, and the animals run to pasture.

sentences.zh: 俗皆髡而衣繡，乘輜軿白蓋小車，出入擊鼓，建旌旗幡幟。

translations.literal: The custom is all to shave the head and wear embroidery, riding covered small carriages with white canopies; going out and coming in they beat drums and raise banners, pennants, and flags.
translations.idiomatic: People shaved their heads and wore embroidered dress, traveling in white-canopied carriages with drums beating and banners flying whenever they went abroad.

sentences.zh: 土多金銀奇寶，有夜光璧、明月珠、駭雞犀、大貝、車渠、瑪瑙、孔翠、珊瑚、琥珀，凡西域諸珍異多出其國。

translations.literal: The soil has much gold, silver, and rare treasures: luminous jade disks, luminous moon pearls, rhinoceros horns that startle chickens, great shells, giant clams, agate, kingfisher feathers, coral, amber—all the rarities of the Western Regions mostly come from this state.
translations.idiomatic: Gold, silver, and exotic treasures abounded—luminous jade, moon pearls, cock-startling rhinoceros horn, giant clams, agate, kingfisher feathers, coral, amber—most of the West's wonders came from Fulin.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝常將通拂菻，竟不能致。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang of Sui often intended to open relations with Fulin but ultimately could not achieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang repeatedly tried to establish contact with Fulin but never succeeded.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十七年，拂菻王波多力遣使獻赤玻璃、綠金精等物，太宗降璽書答慰，賜以綾綺焉。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Zhenguan, the Fulin king Bodoli sent envoys presenting red glass, green gold essence, and other things. Taizong issued an imperial letter in reply to comfort him and bestowed silks.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 17 King Bodoli of Fulin sent red glass, green gold ore, and other gifts; Taizong replied with an imperial letter of reassurance and a gift of silks.

sentences.zh: 自大食強盛，漸陵諸國，乃遣大將軍摩栧伐其都城，因約為和好，請每歲輸之金帛，遂臣屬大食焉。

translations.literal: From the time Dashi grew strong and gradually overawed the various states, it sent the great general Muhan to attack their capital, then made a treaty of friendship requesting yearly tribute of gold and silks, and thus became subject to Dashi.
translations.idiomatic: As the Arabs grew powerful and subjugated neighboring states, they sent General Muhan against the Fulin capital, then imposed a treaty requiring annual tribute of gold and silk; Fulin became a vassal of Dashi.

sentences.zh: 乾封二年，遣使獻底也伽。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianfeng, envoys were sent presenting Dayaga.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianfeng 2 an embassy presented a Dayaga image.

sentences.zh: 大足元年，復遣使來朝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazu, envoys again came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazu 1 another embassy arrived at court.

sentences.zh: 開元七年正月，其主遣吐火羅大首領獻獅子、羚羊各二。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year of Kaiyuan, its ruler sent a great chieftain of Tuhuoluo presenting two lions and two antelopes.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Kaiyuan 7 the ruler sent a Tuhuoluo chieftain with two lions and two antelopes.

sentences.zh: 不數月，又遣大德僧來朝貢。

translations.literal: Within a few months, a great virtuous monk was again sent to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Within months a senior monk arrived with further tribute.

sentences.zh: 大食國

translations.literal: The State of Dashi
translations.idiomatic: Dashi

sentences.zh: 大食國，本在波斯之西。

translations.literal: The state of Dashi originally lay west of Persia.
translations.idiomatic: Dashi originally lay west of Persia.

sentences.zh: 大業中，有波斯胡人牧駝於俱紛摩地那之山，忽有獅子人語謂之曰：「此山西有三穴，穴中大有兵器，汝可取之。

translations.literal: In the Daye era, a Persian Hu man was herding camels at Mount Jufen Modina when suddenly a lion spoke to him in human language, saying: "West of this mountain are three caves; inside the caves are many weapons—you may take them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era a Persian herdsman was tending camels on Mount Jufen Modina when a lion addressed him in human speech: "West of this mountain are three caves filled with weapons. Take them.

sentences.zh: 穴中並有黑石白文，讀之便作王位。」

translations.literal: In the caves there are also black stones with white writing; reading them one may take the royal throne."
translations.idiomatic: Inside are also black stones inscribed in white; whoever reads them may claim the throne."

sentences.zh: 胡人依言，果見穴中有石及槊刃甚多，上有文，教其反叛。

translations.literal: The Hu man followed the words and indeed saw in the caves many stones and spear blades; upon them were writings instructing him to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The herdsman did as told and found many stones and spearheads bearing inscriptions that commanded rebellion.

sentences.zh: 於是糾合亡命，渡恆曷水，劫奪商旅，其眾漸盛，遂割據波斯西境，自立為王。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gathered fugitives, crossed the Henyi River, plundered merchants and travelers, and his followers gradually grew strong; he then carved out the western border of Persia and established himself as king.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered outlaws, crossed the Henyi River, and preyed on merchants until his band grew strong enough to seize Persia's western marches and proclaim himself king.

sentences.zh: 波斯、拂菻各遣兵討之，皆為所敗。

translations.literal: Persia and Fulin each sent troops to attack him, but all were defeated by him.
translations.idiomatic: Persia and Fulin sent armies against him, but he defeated them both.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年，始遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui, envoys were first sent to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 2 Dashi first sent tribute envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 其王姓大食氏，名噉密莫末膩，自云有國已三十四年，歷三主矣。

translations.literal: Its king bears the surname of the Dashi clan; his name is Tanmi Momoni, and he says the state has already existed thirty-four years and passed through three rulers.
translations.idiomatic: The king bore the royal clan name of Dashi; he was called Tanmi Momoni and said his realm had stood thirty-four years under three successive rulers.

sentences.zh: 其國男兒色黑多須，鼻大而長，似婆羅門；

translations.literal: The men of the state are dark in color with abundant beards, noses large and long, resembling Brahmins;
translations.idiomatic: The men were dark-skinned and heavily bearded, with large long noses rather like Brahmins;

sentences.zh: 婦人白皙。

translations.literal: women are fair and white.
translations.idiomatic: the women fair and pale.

sentences.zh: 亦有文字。

translations.literal: They also have writing.
translations.idiomatic: They had a written language as well.

sentences.zh: 出駝馬，大於諸國。

translations.literal: They produce camels and horses, larger than those of other states.
translations.idiomatic: Their camels and horses surpassed those of other lands.

sentences.zh: 兵刃勁利。

translations.literal: Weapons and blades are keen and strong.
translations.idiomatic: Their arms were exceptionally sharp and strong.

sentences.zh: 其俗勇於戰鬥，好事天神。

translations.literal: Their custom is brave in battle and devoted to the heavenly god.
translations.idiomatic: They were fierce in battle and devout toward their heavenly god.

sentences.zh: 土多沙石，不堪耕種，唯食駝馬等肉。

translations.literal: The soil has much sand and stone, unsuitable for cultivation; they eat only the flesh of camels, horses, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The land was mostly sand and rock, fit for neither farming nor much else; they lived chiefly on camel and horse flesh.

sentences.zh: 俱紛摩地那山在國之西南，鄰於大海，其王移穴中黑石置之於國。

translations.literal: Mount Jufen Modina is in the southwest of the state, neighboring the great sea; its king moved the black stone from the cave and placed it in the state.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Jufen Modina stood in the kingdom's southwest near the sea; the king removed the black stone from the cave and enshrined it in his realm.

sentences.zh: 又嘗遣人乘船，將衣糧入海，經八年而未及西岸。

translations.literal: They also once sent men in boats carrying clothes and provisions out to sea; after eight years they had still not reached the western shore.
translations.idiomatic: They once dispatched a ship loaded with provisions; after eight years at sea it had still not reached the western shore.

sentences.zh: 海中見一方石，石上有樹，幹赤葉青，樹上總生小兒；

translations.literal: In the sea they saw a square stone; upon the stone was a tree, trunk red and leaves green, and on the tree infants grew in clusters;
translations.idiomatic: At sea they came upon a square stone bearing a tree with a red trunk and green leaves, its branches thick with infant figures;

sentences.zh: 長六七寸，見人皆笑，動其手腳，頭著樹枝，其使摘取一枝，小兒便死，收在大食王宮。

translations.literal: six or seven cun long, seeing people they all laughed and moved hands and feet; heads attached to branches—when the envoy plucked one branch the infant died; it was collected in the Dashi king's palace.
translations.idiomatic: each six or seven cun tall, laughing and waving at sight of the crew. Rooted by the head to the branches, the infants died when a branch was broken off; one was taken to the Dashi king's palace.

sentences.zh: 又有女國，在其西北，相去三月行。

translations.literal: There is also a state of women in its northwest, separated by three months' travel.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest lay a women's kingdom three months' journey away.

sentences.zh: 龍朔初，擊破波斯，又破拂菻，始有米面之屬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longshuo, they broke Persia and also broke Fulin, and only then had rice and flour and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Longshuo era they conquered Persia and Fulin and only then acquired grain, flour, and similar staples.

sentences.zh: 又將兵南侵婆羅門，吞並諸胡國，勝兵四十余萬。

translations.literal: They again led troops south to invade Brahman, swallowed and annexed the various Hu states, and had victorious troops numbering more than four hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They then marched south against Brahman, annexed the Western kingdoms, and fielded more than four hundred thousand battle-ready troops.

sentences.zh: 長安中，遣使獻良馬。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era, they sent envoys presenting fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era they sent envoys bearing fine horses.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，又獻方物。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyun, they again presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingyun (711) they again sent regional tribute.

sentences.zh: 開元初，遣使來朝，進馬及寶鈿帶等方物。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, they sent envoys to court, presenting horses and jeweled belts and other local products.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan reign they came to court with horses, jeweled belts, and other tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 其使謁見，唯平立不拜，憲司欲糾之，中書令張說奏曰：「大食殊俗，慕義遠來，不可置罪。」

translations.literal: When their envoy had audience, he merely stood level without bowing; the Censorate wished to impeach him; Grand Councilor Zhang Yue memorialized: "Dashi is a peculiar custom; admiring righteousness they came from afar—guilt cannot be laid upon them."
translations.idiomatic: At audience their envoy stood without bowing. The Censorate moved to punish him, but Grand Councilor Zhang Yue argued: "The Arabs follow different customs; they have come from afar out of respect for our virtue—we cannot treat this as a crime.

sentences.zh: 上特許之。」

translations.literal: The emperor specially permitted it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted an exception.

sentences.zh: 尋又遣使朝獻，自云在本國惟拜天神，雖見王亦無致拜之法，所司屢詰責之，其使遂請依漢法致拜。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they again sent envoys with tribute; they said that in their state they bow only to the Heavenly God—even seeing a king there is no method of bowing; the responsible offices repeatedly questioned and reproved them, and the envoys thereupon requested to bow according to Han methods.
translations.idiomatic: Later envoys explained that at home they bowed only to Heaven—even before their own king they did not prostrate. Officials pressed them repeatedly until the envoys asked to follow Chinese court etiquette.

sentences.zh: 其時西域康國、石國之類，皆臣屬之。

translations.literal: At that time the Western Region states such as Kang and Shi were all its subjects.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Sogdian states of Kang, Shi, and the like had all submitted to them.

sentences.zh: 其境東西萬里，東與突騎施相接焉。

translations.literal: Its territory extended ten thousand li east to west; in the east it adjoined the Turgesh.
translations.idiomatic: Their realm stretched ten thousand li from east to west, bordering the Turgesh in the east.

sentences.zh: 一云隋開皇中，大食族中有孤列種代為酋長，孤列種中又有兩姓：一號盆泥奚深，一號盆泥末換。

translations.literal: One account says that in the Kaihuang era of Sui, among the Dashi tribes the Gulie clan in succession served as chieftains; within the Gulie clan were two surnames: one called Peni Xishen, one called Peni Mohuan.
translations.idiomatic: Another account holds that in Sui Kaihuang times the Gulie clan among the Arabs held the chieftainship in turn, divided into two lines: Peni Xishen and Peni Mohuan.

sentences.zh: 其奚深後有摩訶末者，勇健多智，眾立之為主，東西征伐，開地三千里，兼克夏臘，一名釤城

translations.literal: After the Xishen line there was one called Mohemo, brave, strong, and full of wisdom; the masses established him as lord; he campaigned east and west, opened territory three thousand li, and also conquered Xiala, also called Shancheng
translations.idiomatic: From the Xishen line arose Mohemo, a man of courage and counsel whom the people made their leader. He campaigned east and west, carving out three thousand li of territory and conquering Xiala, also called Shancheng

sentences.zh: 〈（釤音所鑒反）〉。

translations.literal: The character shan is read suo-jian fan.〉
translations.idiomatic: The name Shancheng is pronounced suo-jian fan.〉

sentences.zh: 摩訶末後十四代，至末換。

translations.literal: Fourteen generations after Mohemo came Mohuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen generations after Mohemo the line reached Mohuan.

sentences.zh: 末換殺其兄伊疾而自立，復殘忍，其下怨之。

translations.literal: Mohuan killed his elder brother Yiji and established himself; again cruel, his subordinates resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Mohuan killed his brother Yiji to seize power and ruled with such cruelty that his followers turned against him.

sentences.zh: 有呼羅珊木粗人並波悉林舉義兵，應者悉令著黑衣，旬月間眾盈數萬。

translations.literal: A man of Khorasan named Mucu and Boshilin raised righteous troops; responders were all ordered to wear black garments; within ten days and a month the masses exceeded tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: A Khorasanian named Mucu and Boshilin raised a revolt; all who joined were commanded to wear black. Within a month their numbers swelled past ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 鼓行而西，生擒末換，殺之。

translations.literal: Beating drums they marched west, captured Mohuan alive, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They marched west with drums beating, took Mohuan alive, and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 遂求得奚深種阿蒲羅拔，立之。

translations.literal: They thereupon sought out Apoluoba of the Xishen clan and established him.
translations.idiomatic: They then found Apoluoba of the Xishen line and enthroned him.

sentences.zh: 末換已前謂之「白衣大食」，自阿蒲羅拔後改為「黑衣大食」。

translations.literal: Before Mohuan they were called the "White-Robed Dashi"; from Apoluoba onward they were changed to the "Black-Robed Dashi."
translations.idiomatic: Before Mohuan they were known as the White-Robed Arabs; after Apoluoba they became the Black-Robed Arabs.

sentences.zh: 阿蒲羅拔卒，立其弟阿蒲恭拂。

translations.literal: Apoluoba died; his younger brother Apugongfu was established.
translations.idiomatic: When Apoluoba died, his brother Apugongfu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 至德初遣使朝貢，代宗時為元帥，亦用其國兵以收兩都。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide they sent envoys with tribute; when Daizong was commander-in-chief, he also used their state's troops to recover the Two Capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhide era they sent tribute missions; when Daizong was supreme commander, he employed Arab troops in the recovery of the two capitals.

sentences.zh: 寶應、大曆中頻遣使來。

translations.literal: During Baoying and Dali they frequently sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoying and Dali eras they sent envoys repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 恭拂卒，子迷地立。

translations.literal: Gongfu died; his son Midi was established.
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu died and his son Midi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 迷地卒，子牟棲立，牟棲卒，弟訶論立。

translations.literal: Midi died; his son Mouqi was established; Mouqi died; his younger brother Helun was established.
translations.idiomatic: Midi was followed by his son Mouqi, and Mouqi by his brother Helun.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，與吐蕃為勍敵。

translations.literal: During Zhenyuan they were fierce enemies of Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyuan era they were formidable foes of Tibet.

sentences.zh: 蕃軍太半西禦大食，故鮮為邊患，其力不足也。

translations.literal: Tibetan armies for the most part faced west to resist Dashi; therefore they rarely became a border affliction—their strength was insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet had to commit most of its forces to the west against the Arabs, so it seldom troubled the Tang frontier—its strength was spent elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 十四年，詔以黑衣大食使含嵯、焉雞、沙北三人並為中郎將，各放還蕃。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, an edict appointed the Black-Robed Dashi envoys Hanzuo, Yanji, and Shabei all as Central Commandants and sent each back to his realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan an edict named the Black-Robed Arab envoys Hanzuo, Yanji, and Shabei central commandants and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：西方之國，綿亙山川，自張騫奉使已來，介子立功之後，通於中國者多矣。

translations.literal: The historian says: The states of the west stretch across mountains and rivers; since Zhang Qian's mission and after Jiezi's achievement of merit, many have communicated with China.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: The western lands stretch across mountains and rivers. Since Zhang Qian's mission and Jiezi's exploit, countless peoples have opened ties with China.

sentences.zh: 有唐拓境，遠極安西，弱者德以懷之，強者力以制之。

translations.literal: The Tang expanded its borders, reaching far to Anxi; the weak were embraced through virtue, the strong controlled through force.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang pushed its frontiers to distant Anxi, winning the weak through virtue and the strong through force.

sentences.zh: 開元之前，貢輸不絕。

translations.literal: Before Kaiyuan, tribute and transport did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Kaiyuan era tribute flowed without cease.

sentences.zh: 天寶之亂，邊僥多虞，邠郊之西，即為戎狄，槁街之邸，來朝亦稀。

translations.literal: In the disorders of Tianbao, the border marches had many alarms; west of Bin and the suburbs were already Rong and Di; at the lodges of Gaojie, those coming to court were also few.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianbao rebellion brought constant alarms on the frontier; west of Bin lay only barbarian lands, and the guest lodges at court saw ever fewer visitors.

sentences.zh: 故古先哲王，務寧華夏，語曰：「近者悅，遠者來。」

translations.literal: Therefore the sage kings of antiquity strove to bring peace to Huaxia; the saying goes: "When those near are pleased, those far come."
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings of old sought tranquility for the Central Realm, as the proverb says: "Make the near content, and the distant will come.

sentences.zh: 斯之謂矣！

translations.literal: This is what is meant!
translations.idiomatic: This is precisely what was meant!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：大蒙之人，西方之國，與時盛衰，隨世通塞。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The people of great Meng, states of the west—rise and fall with the times, open and close with the age.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: The peoples of the great west rise and fall with the times, their roads to China opening and closing with the age.

sentences.zh: 勿謂戎心，不懷我德；

translations.literal: Do not say the Rong heart does not cherish our virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Do not suppose the barbarian heart incapable of honoring our virtue;

sentences.zh: 貞觀、開元，槁街充斥。

translations.literal: in Zhenguan and Kaiyuan, Gaojie lodges were packed full.
translations.idiomatic: under Zhenguan and Kaiyuan the court's guest lodges overflowed with visitors.
